rules.title: Check the critical drainage area boundary
rules.text: Use the Torbay CDA criteria for conservative screening across Torbay. For a site in Maidencombe, establish the current EA designation and boundary before relying on CDA status in a formal assessment.
rules.when: All development that could affect drainage.
rules.check: The site against the current designation map, the applicable local policy and any written confirmation of the 2026 extension. Record the boundary and the basis of the assessment.
rules.note: Sources differ. The Local Plan (2015) and SFRA Level 1 (June 2026) say the whole of Torbay is a CDA. The Validation List (November 2024) and the draft SFRA Level 2A (June 2026) say Maidencombe is outside it. The EA national dataset published in September 2026 has a July 2025 geometry revision and does not establish the extension. Whole-Torbay screening is the working interpretation, not confirmation of a new formal boundary. The local Validation List still requires an FRA in Maidencombe.
evidence: Dated designation map and recorded assessment basis
Locate the application boundary and identify the source version. For Maidencombe, record the published source difference and the confirmation relied on.
A general statement that the whole borough is designated, without addressing the boundary evidence.

rules.title: Seek a contribution to wider flood risk reduction
rules.text: Development in the CDA should be served by SuDS meeting the CDA criteria and should also contribute to a scheme that reduces risk for those liable to flood, for example by improving a constrained channel, culvert or bridge.
rules.when: New development in the CDA, proportionate to scale.
rules.check: Whether the proposal identifies or contributes to a downstream improvement. ER1 allows a financial contribution to be requested.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
Whether the proposal identifies or contributes to a downstream improvement. ER1 allows a financial contribution to be requested.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Require a flood risk assessment with a surface water drainage strategy
rules.text: A flood risk assessment (FRA), including a surface water drainage strategy, is a local validation requirement for householder, full, outline and reserved matters applications and relevant demolition in a conservation area.
rules.when: All listed application types anywhere in Torbay. For prior approvals, compare Validation List 4.1.4 and 4.2.15 and record the applicable planning class, submission scope and assessment basis. Their stated scopes differ; seek Council clarification where applicability is uncertain.
rules.check: That an FRA is submitted before validation. Householder development in Flood Zone 1 can normally use the short Torbay proforma.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
That an FRA is submitted before validation. Householder development in Flood Zone 1 can normally use the short Torbay proforma.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Require a site-specific FRA where NPPF F4 applies
rules.text: A site-specific FRA should accompany development proposals in Flood Zones 2, 3a and 3b. In Flood Zone 1, it should inform and accompany proposals on sites of 1 ha or more, land the EA has identified as having critical drainage problems, or land identified in an SFRA or the Flood Map for Planning as being at risk from any source now or in future.
rules.when: Any development meeting an F4 trigger. Confirm the current EA-designated boundary where that trigger is material; local FRA requirements also apply.
rules.check: The F4 trigger and evidence, and an FRA proportionate to the scale, nature and location of the development, covering relevant flood sources, future climate and lifetime.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment
Identify the F4 trigger from the flood zone, site area, EA designation or SFRA/Flood Map evidence. Trace relevant flood sources, future conditions and lifetime through the proportionate assessment.
A single Flood Zone image or an assessment that omits the relevant source or trigger.

rules.title: Check the Local Plan FRA level
rules.text: A basic FRA for all development; a more detailed FRA for Flood Zone 1 sites of 1 ha or more (including those draining into Flood Zones 2 and 3), all new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3, and development near seafronts at risk from wave action.
rules.check: That the depth of the FRA matches the ER1 category.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
That the depth of the FRA matches the ER1 category.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Apply the sequential test
rules.text: Steer development to the lowest flood risk land where suitable alternative sites are reasonably available. Torbay's Validation List includes a flooding sequential test for new dwellings in Flood Zones 2 and 3. Check the current national exemptions and the applicable local requirements.
rules.when: Development at risk now or in future from any source, unless an exemption in NPPF F5.2 is demonstrated.
rules.check: That the sequential test is passed or the precise F5.2 exemption is supported by evidence. The test area should not exceed the anticipated catchment of the development's occupiers or users.
rules.note: F5.2 exempts allocated sites tested during plan preparation; sites where an FRA clearly demonstrates that no built development, access or escape routes, land raising or other vulnerable elements are on land at risk now or in future; or surface-water-only risk where layout, design and mitigation meet F7 lifetime safety without increasing risk elsewhere. It also exempts householder development, non-residential extensions with a footprint less than 250 m², and changes of use other than to caravan, camping, chalet, mobile home or park home sites.
evidence: Sequential-test evidence or precise exemption
Match the proposal and FRA to the relevant F5.2 exemption, or demonstrate the sequential test using suitable reasonably available alternatives and the appropriate catchment.
An obsolete change-of-use exemption or an unsupported assertion that the site is exempt.

rules.title: Check flood-zone compatibility and the exception test
rules.text: Check the use against NPPF Annex F tables 2 and 3: incompatible development should be refused. Where the exception test applies, demonstrate wider sustainability benefits that outweigh flood risk, lifetime safety under F7, and no increase in flood risk elsewhere with an overall reduction where possible.
rules.when: Development in Flood Zones 2, 3a or 3b; the exception-test requirement depends on vulnerability and the exemptions in NPPF F6.2.
rules.check: Flood-zone and vulnerability classification, compatibility, all three exception-test criteria supported by the FRA, or the evidenced F6.2 exemption.
rules.note: F6.2 removes the exception-test requirement for forms or circumstances exempt from the sequential test under F5, and for allocated sites tested at plan-making stage unless flood risk has since significantly increased or the proposal has changed significantly to introduce a more vulnerable use. This does not remove the separate flood-zone compatibility check.
evidence: Flood-zone compatibility and exception-test evidence
Check Annex F classification and compatibility first, then all three F6.1 criteria or the precise F6.2 exception-test exemption.
A passed exception test used to justify an incompatible use, or a missing lifetime-safety or off-site-risk criterion.

rules.title: Make development safe from flooding
rules.text: Development should not present a flood risk to occupiers, users or visitors or increase flood risk elsewhere. Where risk exists now or in future, locate the most vulnerable development in the lowest risk areas unless overriding reasons justify otherwise. Demonstrate lifetime safety for its users, safe management of residual risk and, where appropriate, safe access and escape as part of an agreed emergency plan. Provide flood resistance and resilience allowing rapid return to use without significant refurbishment.
rules.when: All development at risk of flooding now or in future.
rules.check: Siting and any overriding reasons, lifetime safety, finished floor levels, residual risk, the applicable emergency plan and access arrangements, resilience and effects elsewhere.
evidence: Lifetime safety, residual-risk and resilience evidence
Relate the layout, any overriding siting reasons, user vulnerability, applicable emergency plan, access, resilience and effects elsewhere to the assessed present and future flood conditions.
Safe access asserted without the relevant emergency arrangements, or resilience described without an effective return-to-use outcome.

rules.title: Set finished floor levels above the design flood level
rules.text: Set finished floor levels above the 1 in 100 year flood level, with climate change, where the site is at risk.
rules.check: Floor levels against modelled flood levels.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
Floor levels against modelled flood levels.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Coastal change and future tidal inundation
rules.text: NPPF F9 covers coastal change management areas and other areas likely to face coastal erosion or tidal inundation over the next century. Demonstrate lifetime safety, consistency with the relevant Shoreline Management Plan without unacceptable effects on coastal change processes, and wider sustainability benefits that justify development. Torbay's Validation List requires a coastal change vulnerability assessment within a coastal change management area.
rules.when: Sites within a coastal change management area or other areas within the national F9 risk scope.
rules.check: The national coastal-erosion map and current local evidence, all F9 criteria, any applicable local vulnerability-assessment requirement and drainage effects on coastal stability.
evidence: Coastal-risk scope and assessment evidence

Check mapped coastal change management areas and the wider national F9 coastal-erosion or tidal-inundation scope. Demonstrate all F9 criteria and the local validation assessment where its trigger applies.
A site outside a mapped coastal change management area treated as automatically outside national F9.

rules.title: No basement accommodation where there is danger of inundation
rules.text: Basement accommodation, including changes of use or basement parking, will not be permitted where there is danger of inundation and risk to life.
rules.when: Proposals with basements in areas at risk.
rules.check: Basement flood risk in the FRA.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
Basement flood risk in the FRA.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Use the 2026 SFRA maps
rules.text: Check the SFRA surface water maps (current and future) and the Flood Zone 3b map, alongside the EA Flood map for planning.
rules.check: That the FRA uses the current SFRA mapping, not superseded 2008 or 2010 data.
evidence: Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant
That the FRA uses the current SFRA mapping, not superseded 2008 or 2010 data.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Follow the destination hierarchy
rules.text: Discharge runoff to the following destinations, to the maximum extent practicable, in this order: 1 collect for non-potable use; 2 infiltrate to ground; 3 discharge to an above-ground surface water body; 4 discharge to a surface water sewer or other piped surface water system; 5 discharge to a combined sewer.
rules.check: That each higher destination has been assessed and used as far as practicable.
rules.note: The Local Plan (2015) and the Torbay guide (2022) start the hierarchy at infiltration. The national standards (2025) put reuse first. Reuse first is the current national position in standard 1.2.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
That each higher destination has been assessed and used as far as practicable.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Evidence for using a lower destination
rules.text: Evidence shall show all higher priority destinations have been used to the maximum extent practicable. Higher cost alone is not a reason to use a lower destination.
rules.check: Site evidence (tests, levels, distances), not assertion or cost alone.
evidence: Destination appraisal
For each higher destination, identify the site evidence, practicable use and reason any remaining runoff needs a lower destination.
A conclusion that infiltration is unsuitable without the supporting assessment.

rules.title: Maximise each destination in order
rules.text: Where more than one destination is used, maximise each one's ability to accept runoff in order of priority.
rules.check: The proportion of area to each destination.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
The proportion of area to each destination.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Contamination is not an automatic reason to move down
rules.text: Do not discount higher priority destinations because a site is or was contaminated where practicable remediation can be designed with the drainage.
rules.check: That remediation and drainage options were considered together.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
That remediation and drainage options were considered together.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Secure rights over third-party land
rules.text: Where discharge needs third-party land, provide evidence of easements for the lifetime of the development.
rules.when: Outfalls or routes across land not owned by the applicant.
rules.check: Easement or agreement evidence. Where rights cannot be obtained, the council may have powers under FWMA 2010 Schedule 2 paragraph 29(1).
evidence: Land-rights evidence and route plan
Match the proposed connection and access route to the land affected and the rights needed for construction, use and maintenance.
A drainage line crossing third-party land with no evidence of the necessary rights.

rules.title: No increase in flood risk elsewhere
rules.text: Runoff from the development shall not increase flood risk elsewhere from any source.
rules.check: Downstream effects, adjacent land and the receiving system.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Downstream effects, adjacent land and the receiving system.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: No depletion of waters
rules.text: The design shall not deplete surface waters or groundwater beyond safe environmental levels.
rules.when: Schemes that divert runoff away from its natural catchment or receiving water.
rules.check: That natural catchments are replicated as far as practicable.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
That natural catchments are replicated as far as practicable.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Keep surface water out of foul sewers
rules.text: Essentially uncontaminated surface water shall not discharge to a foul-only sewer. The national standards except runoff integral to a foul pumping station. Very contaminated runoff is dealt with separately under the water quality requirements, including any consent for foul discharge.
rules.check: The runoff type, sewer classification, connection drawings and any consent for the exceptional discharge.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
The runoff type, sewer classification, connection drawings and any consent for the exceptional discharge.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Consider rainwater harvesting
rules.text: Rainwater harvesting shall be considered where there is a non-potable demand with enough catchment, a need for landscape irrigation, or the area is seriously water stressed.
rules.when: Any of the three triggers applies. Examples include industrial, commercial, educational, public sector, residential and multiple-occupancy buildings.
rules.check: A reasoned demand assessment. If harvesting is not used, the reason.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
A reasoned demand assessment. If harvesting is not used, the reason.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Design rainwater harvesting for its intended use
rules.text: Harvesting used to manage large rainfall events shall be designed to BS EN 16941. Harvesting design shall follow best practice and demonstrate effectiveness against a rainfall time series. Communal systems outside the curtilage shall consider public health and security.
rules.when: Rainwater harvesting is proposed; apply the large-event and communal-system conditions where relevant.
rules.check: Rainfall time series, demand profile, applicable design standard and public health and security assessment.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Rainfall time series, demand profile, applicable design standard and public health and security assessment.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Agree discharge to a watercourse in writing
rules.text: The principle of discharge to an above-ground water body, including rates and volumes, shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authority. This does not replace permits or consents.
rules.check: Written agreement in principle; ordinary watercourse consent or EA permit as needed.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Written agreement in principle; ordinary watercourse consent or EA permit as needed.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Agree sewer connections in writing with capacity
rules.text: Discharge to a surface water sewer, other piped drainage or combined sewer shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authorities and the downstream owner if different. Include rates, volumes, connection location and confirmation of capacity.
rules.check: Written agreements from the relevant authorities and owner; capacity evidence and the proposed connection point.
evidence: Written connection and capacity evidence
Check the receiving system, location, proposed discharge and the agreed capacity basis against the submitted design.
An enquiry acknowledgement or a sewer-location plan used as connection approval.

rules.title: Combined sewer: control to greenfield and assess pollution
rules.text: A combined sewer is the last destination in the hierarchy. ER2 requires greenfield discharge rates. Assess pollution from surcharge or flooding of the receiving combined sewer and provide mitigation demonstrating that pollution risk is not increased. Where capacity is insufficient, the developer should work with the undertaker to fund capacity.
rules.check: Hierarchy evidence, greenfield rate, receiving sewer capacity, pollution assessment and effective mitigation.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Hierarchy evidence, greenfield rate, receiving sewer capacity, pollution assessment and effective mitigation.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Torquay: appropriate assessment where the hierarchy is not met
rules.text: In Torquay, development that has not met the ER2 drainage hierarchy will be subject to an individual Habitats Regulations Appropriate Assessment.
rules.when: Torquay sites that do not meet the hierarchy.
rules.check: Refer to the council ecologist.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Refer to the council ecologist.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Pumping by exception only
rules.text: Pumping shall be by exception and agreed with the approving body. Assess pumping against a lower destination reachable by gravity, including cost, failure risk, pollution and flooding. Pump only the parts that cannot drain by gravity.
rules.check: The gravity alternative, the area pumped and the failure assessment.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
The gravity alternative, the area pumped and the failure assessment.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Pumping station design and downstream capacity
rules.text: Design pumping stations to recognised guidance unless an alternative is agreed in writing with the proposed adoption organisation and the approving body if different. Where a downstream pumping station receives the flow, provide written confirmation of capacity from its owner.
rules.when: Pumped systems or downstream pumping stations.
rules.check: Design standard and owner capacity letter.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
Design standard and owner capacity letter.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Ask for a fallback destination
rules.text: Ask for a fallback (Plan B) destination if infiltration proves unsuitable at detailed design or a connection is refused.
rules.when: Outline and full applications relying on infiltration or an unconfirmed connection.
rules.check: A deliverable fallback that still meets the discharge limits.
evidence: Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights
A deliverable fallback that still meets the discharge limits.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Prove infiltration with site testing
rules.text: Infiltration depends on suitable ground and adequate tested rates. Geotechnical investigation shall confirm the ground is suitable using recognised methods. Mapping can form an initial evidence base.
rules.when: Infiltration proposed, or evidence needed to assess its feasibility. Mapping can inform whether ground investigation is necessary.
rules.check: Adequate site evidence for the hierarchy decision; location-specific investigation and testing where infiltration is relied on.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Adequate site evidence for the hierarchy decision; location-specific investigation and testing where infiltration is relied on.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Test to BRE 365 at the feature location and depth
rules.text: Test in strict accordance with BRE 365 at the location and depth of each feature (or within 20 m where results are similar). Three consecutive tests to near emptying; extrapolation from 25% effective depth is not accepted. Permeable paving tested at 20 m intervals with pits at least 1.5 m × 1 m.
rules.check: Test locations against the layout; three fills; full drainage.
evidence: Test plan and test records
Match test locations, depths, logs and adopted infiltration rate to the proposed feature. Read the Torbay test criterion alongside the detailed ground evidence.
Unlocated test results or a test depth unrelated to the feature base.

rules.title: Keep 1 m above maximum groundwater
rules.text: The base of infiltration features shall be at least 1 m above the maximum likely groundwater level. For systems wholly relying on infiltration this 1 m unsaturated zone also protects groundwater.
rules.check: Base level against groundwater evidence.
evidence: Groundwater evidence and feature section
Show maximum likely groundwater and the proposed base on the same datum, with the separation demonstrated.
Groundwater depth quoted without relating it to the feature base.

rules.title: Establish wet-winter groundwater levels
rules.text: Confirm groundwater levels through investigation during high groundwater periods, using records at or near the site, with enough data to show seasonal levels.
rules.check: Monitoring period and season. Single dry-season readings are not enough.
rules.note: There is no Torbay rule for the monitoring period. Devon asks for monitoring over November to May (reference only).
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Monitoring period and season. Single dry-season readings are not enough.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding
rules.text: Infiltration shall not cause unacceptable instability or subsidence (including riverbanks and coastal features), groundwater or surface water pollution, groundwater flooding, or ingress to foul or combined sewers.
rules.check: Ground risk assessment. Torbay guide 4.2 lists slopes over 10%, unstable or contaminated ground, services and proximity.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Ground risk assessment. Torbay guide 4.2 lists slopes over 10%, unstable or contaminated ground, services and proximity.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Deep-bore infiltration by exception
rules.text: Deep-bore infiltration is not a SuDS approach. It shall be by exception with an agreement in principle from the relevant risk management authority.
rules.check: Exceptional justification and EA agreement or permit.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Exceptional justification and EA agreement or permit.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Do not rely only on point infiltration below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s
rules.text: Point infiltration (for example soakaways) shall not be fully relied on where infiltration rates are below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s.
rules.check: Tested rate. If lower, an additional destination.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Tested rate. If lower, an additional destination.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Half-empty within 24 hours
rules.text: Infiltration features shall half-empty their runoff volume within 24 hours for events up to the 3.3% AEP event.
rules.check: Half-drain time in the calculations.
evidence: Infiltration storage and half-drain calculation
Identify the tested rate, storage geometry and safety factor used to demonstrate the stated half-drain performance.
A storage-volume result without a drain-time check.

rules.title: Use the Torbay factor of safety
rules.text: Size infiltration with the RP156 factor of safety. Torbay expects the 'minor damage to external areas or inconvenience' values: 2 for areas under 100 m², 3 for 100 to 1000 m², 5 for over 1000 m². Use 10 where failure would damage buildings or cause major inconvenience.
rules.when: Infiltration designed with the RP156 (CIRIA) method.
rules.check: Factor used against drained area and consequence.
evidence: Calculation input and consequence assessment
Trace the RP156 factor to the drained area and consequence of failure, and check it is applied in the calculation.
A factor stated in the narrative but absent or different in the calculation.

rules.title: Assess point infiltration within 5 m of structures
rules.text: Where runoff goes to point infiltration within 5 m of existing or proposed buildings, roads, embankments or other infrastructure, assess instability and mitigate. Unstable geology may need more than 5 m.
rules.check: Distances on the layout and the stability assessment.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Distances on the layout and the stability assessment.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Assess diffuse infiltration within 3 m of buildings
rules.text: Diffuse near-surface infiltration taking direct rainfall or a very small catchment similar in area to the infiltration surface should not normally pose a structural risk. Such proposals within 3 m of a building shall be assessed and mitigated where required. This reassurance does not extend to large contributing catchments.
rules.when: Permeable surfaces or similar within 3 m of a building.
rules.check: Distance, contributing area relative to the infiltration surface, ground conditions, structural risk and any mitigation.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Distance, contributing area relative to the infiltration surface, ground conditions, structural risk and any mitigation.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Protect infiltration surfaces from clogging
rules.text: Features that infiltrate should include or be preceded by pre-treatment that protects the infiltration surface.
rules.check: Silt traps, filter strips or other pre-treatment.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Silt traps, filter strips or other pre-treatment.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Groundwater protection and contaminated land
rules.text: Follow EA groundwater protection guidance when discharging to ground. Infiltration through contaminated land is allowed only where there is no risk of mobilising pollutants.
rules.when: Infiltration, especially on brownfield land or in source protection zones.
rules.check: Groundwater risk assessment.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Groundwater risk assessment.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Structural loading below trafficked surfaces
rules.text: Where infiltration lies beneath trafficked surfaces, consider structural loading and soil weakening when saturated.
rules.check: Structural design note.
evidence: Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations
Structural design note.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Intercept the first 5 mm
rules.text: Deliver interception within the development so the first 5 mm of rainfall produces no runoff for at least 80% of summer events (May to October) and 50% of winter events (November to April).
rules.check: Interception method for every positively drained surface.
evidence: Surface-by-surface interception schedule
Identify each positively drained surface, its receiving feature, the loss or reuse mechanism and the evidence supporting it.
One site-wide assertion that all SuDS provide interception.

rules.title: Design interception with quality, amenity and biodiversity
rules.text: Show the everyday rainfall approach was developed alongside water quality, amenity and biodiversity.
rules.check: That interception features are part of the landscape and treatment train.
evidence: Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement
That interception features are part of the landscape and treatment train.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Deemed compliance: harvesting
rules.text: Optional deemed-compliance route: a development is deemed compliant if rainwater harvesting means no runoff leaves the development for lower-order events, shown by BS EN 16941 calculations. This does not require the feature to be provided.
rules.check: BS EN 16941 calculations.
evidence: Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement
BS EN 16941 calculations.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Deemed compliance: full infiltration of monthly events
rules.text: Optional deemed-compliance route: a development is deemed compliant if it infiltrates entirely to ground so no runoff leaves for events with a 1 in 1 or greater chance each month, shown by calculations and infiltration tests. A soakaway designed for 1 in 1 or 1 in 10 year events already meets this. This does not require the feature to be provided.
rules.check: Infiltration calculations and tests.
evidence: Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement
Infiltration calculations and tests.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Simplified approach needs agreement
rules.text: Where no modelling is used, the simplified approach (features and ratios in 2.7) may be accepted with the approving body's agreement. Where a feature lacks capacity, downstream features can add it, with detailed calculations.
rules.check: That 2.7 presumptions are met exactly.
evidence: Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement
That 2.7 presumptions are met exactly.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Green roofs and walls
rules.text: Surfaces with green roofs or walls that drain only their own area comply.
rules.check: That no other area drains onto the roof.
rules.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.
evidence: Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement
That no other area drains onto the roof.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Rainwater harvesting and water butts
rules.text: Surfaces draining to BS EN 16941 harvesting based on regular daily non-potable demand comply. Water butts limited to garden use in dry periods do not.
rules.check: Daily demand basis; water butts not counted unless designed with calculations.
rules.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.
evidence: Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement
Daily demand basis; water butts not counted unless designed with calculations.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Permeable surfaces
rules.text: No added area: complies (lined or unlined). Unlined with added impermeable area no greater than the permeable area: complies. Unlined over ground above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 5× the permeable area may be added (100 m² impermeable needs 20 m² permeable). Lined with added area: does not comply; add downstream interception.
rules.check: Lining, added area ratio and tested rate.
rules.nums: 1:1 unlined · 5:1 if k > 1×10⁻⁶ m/s · lined + added area fails
rules.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.
evidence: Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement

rules.title: Swales
rules.text: Fall under 1:100 with at least 500 mm suitable base: up to 5× the vegetated base area. Unlined, fall under 1:100 and over 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 25×. Steeper than 1:100: no interception unless shown by design. Areas draining within 5 m of an unlined swale outlet do not count unless the swale is flat with a raised outlet.
rules.check: Long-section fall, base material, lining and outlet arrangement.
rules.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.

rules.title: Detention basins
rules.text: A flat, unlined vegetated basin base below the outlet, without specific provision routing low flows directly to the outlet, can receive up to five times that base area. Above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s infiltration, the ratio can be up to 25:1. Higher ratios need justification using below-outlet storage, higher infiltration rates and detailed design. Provide upstream sediment control for infiltrating basins.

rules.note: This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7.
evidence: Basin catchment plan and section
Identify effective receiving area, lining, infiltration, low-flow route and levels below the outlet. Test every applicable basin condition.

rules.text: All off-site discharges should mimic greenfield performance up to a maximum of the 1 in 10 year greenfield rate. Where infiltration is not suitable, limit flows to the 1 in 10 year greenfield rate.

rules.title: 50% AEP limit
rules.text: Limit the 50% AEP peak to the 50% AEP greenfield rate (Qbar or Qmed) or 3 l/s/ha, whichever is greater.

rules.title: 1% AEP limit: volume test
rules.text: Compare the volume discharged to surface waters or sewers in the developed 1% AEP 6-hour event with greenfield runoff volume for the same event. If greater, limit the 1% AEP peak to max(the 50% AEP greenfield rate, 3 l/s/ha). If equal or less, limit it to max(the 1% AEP greenfield rate, 3 l/s/ha). Distinguish runoff generated from the volume remaining to be discharged after interception, reuse or infiltration.
rules.when: Discharge to surface waters or sewers.
rules.check: The 6-hour discharged-volume comparison, its contributing area and the national branch used.
evidence: Greenfield runoff and developed discharged-volume comparison

Compare the same 1% AEP, six-hour event and contributing area. Identify the developed volume discharged to surface waters or sewers after interception, reuse or infiltration, then select the correct national discharge-limit branch.

rules.title: Compare the applicable national and local limits
rules.text: Calculate the national 50% AEP limit and the correct 1% AEP volume branch. Separately show the applicable local greenfield performance and Q10 ceiling. Use the more stringent applicable criterion for each event where the evidence-based local approach satisfies national standard 3.10. Do not raise a calculated limit automatically to 1.5 l/s.
rules.when: Positive discharges where national and local criteria overlap.
rules.check: Use the runoff comparison; record the local policy basis, the governing event and any agreed departure.
rules.note: National 3.10 gives a more stringent, evidence-based local approach precedence. Torbay guide 3.5 says the CDA criteria take preference where they overlap. The CDA's 'mimic greenfield' has no 3 l/s/ha floor, so for small or low-runoff sites it is stricter than national 3.18.
evidence: National and local event comparison
Show each applicable limit, its event, site scope and policy basis. Record how a source difference or agreement affects the chosen criterion.

rules.title: Check proposals relying on the published 1.5 l/s minimum
rules.text: The September 2022 Torbay guide states a minimum positive discharge of 1.5 l/s. Where that exceeds a current national or applicable local limit, record the conflict and obtain the approving body's agreement to the proposed approach.

rules.check: The lower calculated limit, evidence for the proposed control, blockage protection and the recorded approval or departure.
rules.note: This published local minimum is not a national exemption. It can conflict with low greenfield rates on sites of different sizes. The comparison tool leaves the conflict visible.

rules.title: Tidal or sea outfalls

rules.title: Greenfield runoff method
rules.text: Estimate greenfield rates with the EA Flood Estimation Guidelines, using the whole area that could drain to the system (permeable and impermeable), with soil parameters confirmed by ground investigation. Recommendation (3.30): calculate baseline greenfield rates and volumes without a climate change allowance.

rules.title: Climate change: upper end allowance
rules.text: Use the latest EA allowances, upper end, for the epoch matching the design life. Torbay (South Devon catchment), 2070s epoch (2061 to 2125): +40% for 3.3% AEP and +50% for 1% AEP. 2050s epoch (2022 to 2060): +35% and +45%. Record the development's lifetime and how it is covered by the selected epoch.
rules.check: Allowance and epoch against the design life.
rules.note: National SuDS standard 3.8 specifies the upper-end allowance for drainage design. EA general surface-water FRA guidance separately describes central allowances for shorter lifetimes; do not substitute those for the national SuDS design requirement. The Torbay guide's 50% matches the 2070s upper end for the 1% event. For a shorter-lifetime proposal where the current national allowance is lower, record how the published local 50% criterion is applied and obtain agreement for the assessment basis.
evidence: Lifetime and climate input schedule

rules.title: Management and maintenance plan
rules.text: Provide a management and maintenance plan that sustains performance against standards 1–6 for the development’s lifetime. Torbay asks for the plan and an inspection checklist. The detailed management and maintenance contents in national standards 7.10–7.11 are recommendations.
rules.when: All applicable development; establish the delivery arrangements at outline and supply detail appropriate to the application stage.
rules.check: Responsibilities and funding; asset and land ownership; easements; operating and pollution-incident instructions; establishment and routine maintenance; inspections, sediment and pollution controls and disposal; remedial work, replacement and post-flood rehabilitation.
evidence: Asset-specific management and maintenance plan
Identify each asset, responsible party, lifetime arrangements and practical maintenance. Use the recommended contents in their stated context.
A generic schedule with no asset ownership or delivery arrangements.

rules.title: Consider failure scenarios
rules.text: Examine the likelihood and consequences of operational failure, including blocked structures and controls and failed pumps. Evaluate both flood risk and water quality impacts and manage the risks. The design should make consequential blockage or clogging apparent from surface inspection.
rules.check: Flood-risk and water-quality failure assessment, safe operation and the means of detecting failure.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Flood-risk and water-quality failure assessment, safe operation and the means of detecting failure.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Access for maintenance
rules.text: Allow free, safe and easy access (with easements) for people, vehicles and machinery, including for emergencies.
rules.check: Access routes on the layout.
evidence: Maintenance access plan and sections
Check that the maintenance activity and required equipment can reach each asset using the proposed route and rights.
A route labelled “access” without considering the actual task or obstructions.

rules.title: Sediment removal
rules.text: Design the system so sediment, detritus and debris can be easily removed. Easily emptied, replaced or rehabilitated sediment controls are recommended where deposits could harm performance or design life. Establish the lawful waste classification, handling and disposal route for removed material.
rules.check: Access, sediment controls, removal method, waste classification and the applicable disposal requirements.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Access, sediment controls, removal method, waste classification and the applicable disposal requirements.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Automatic monitoring of pumps and proprietary products
rules.text: Where pumps or proprietary below-ground products (for example separators) are used, provide automatic monitoring and failure warnings to the responsible body.
rules.check: Telemetry specification.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Telemetry specification.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Performance monitoring
rules.text: Monitoring may be needed depending on scale and risk. Agree it with the approving body.
rules.check: Monitoring provisions.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Monitoring provisions.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Minimise energy and prioritise source control
rules.text: As far as reasonably practicable, minimise energy use over the design life. Prioritise source control to minimise large downstream attenuation ponds with safety-critical maintenance requirements.
rules.check: Distribution of features; pumping avoided.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Distribution of features; pumping avoided.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Ecology in maintenance
rules.text: Reference ecological surveys in maintenance planning. Consider invasive species and biosecurity in vegetation management.
rules.check: Maintenance plan ecology section.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Maintenance plan ecology section.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Construction information and phasing
rules.text: Give the contractor information on protecting and commissioning drainage during construction. For phased developments, provide a phased plan showing flow control in each phase.
rules.check: Construction drainage plan; phasing plan.
evidence: Construction and phasing information
Explain temporary drainage, protection of infiltration and treatment surfaces, and how each phase remains operational.
Only the final layout shown, with no treatment of construction runoff or incomplete phases.

rules.title: Build to the approved design
rules.text: Construct in strict accordance with the design. Report discrepancies to the designer and the council. The council may inspect and may take enforcement action.
rules.check: As-built drawings against the approval.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
As-built drawings against the approval.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: CDM and materials
rules.text: Designers take account of construction, operation, maintenance and decommissioning risks under CDM 2015 and minimise them as far as reasonably practicable. Specify materials suitable for their intended use, having regard to preserving natural resources and minimising embedded carbon.
rules.check: Designer’s risk assessment, operational access and suitable material specifications; no invented carbon threshold.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Designer’s risk assessment, operational access and suitable material specifications; no invented carbon threshold.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Design life and loading
rules.text: Show components last the development's design life (or include replacement in the plan) and resist design loads with factors of safety. Underground storage must suit the final surface use.
rules.check: Product specifications; structural adequacy of crates under parking.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Product specifications; structural adequacy of crates under parking.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: No harm to nearby infrastructure
rules.text: Confirm construction and operation of SuDS do not harm nearby roads, railways or pipelines.
rules.check: Assessment.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Assessment.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Adoption routes
rules.text: Confirm who will own each asset. Sewers: South West Water under a section 104 agreement. Highway drainage: Torbay Highways under section 38, after the section 104 agreement. Other features: management company or owner. Planning approval does not mean the council adopts the system.
rules.check: Agreement in principle and a fallback if adoption is refused.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Agreement in principle and a fallback if adoption is refused.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Register of structures
rules.text: Following adoption, the local planning authority shall inform the lead local flood authority, which shall register the drainage system, including any non-adopted part. Record the adoption and notification arrangements.
rules.when: A drainage system has been adopted.
rules.check: Adoption record, LPA notification to the LLFA and registration covering the whole system.
evidence: Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence
Adoption record, LPA notification to the LLFA and registration covering the whole system.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: SuDS for all development that could affect drainage
rules.text: Development that could affect drainage on or around the site should include SuDS proportionate to its nature and scale, designed to the national standards, with acceptable operation for its lifetime. Major development takes account of LLFA advice.
rules.when: All development that could affect drainage, not only major.
rules.check: Proportionate SuDS for the scale.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant
Proportionate SuDS for the scale.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Statement of how the national standards are met
rules.text: Applications for development that could affect drainage should include a statement of how the national SuDS standards will be achieved.
rules.check: A statement covering all seven standards, proportionate to scale. The EA SuDS Strategy Templates give a ready format.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant
A statement covering all seven standards, proportionate to scale. The EA SuDS Strategy Templates give a ready format.

rules.title: Local Plan ER1 and ER2
rules.text: ER1: development safe for its lifetime, SuDS to restrict discharge rates, no increased discharge from Ilsham CSO, contributions where needed. ER2: water efficiency, protection of waters, pollution prevention plans, separate foul and surface water, and the drainage hierarchy.
rules.check: Policy compliance in the planning assessment.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant

rules.title: Torbay submission list
rules.text: Expect: percolation tests and geotechnical report; one hydraulic model of SuDS and pipes; layout drawings (cover and invert levels, pipe sizes, lengths, gradients, gullies, numbering, catchments); flow control details; SuDS details; construction drawings; maintenance plan and inspection checklist; exceedance and blockage plan; connection permissions; evidence the hierarchy was followed.
rules.check: Each item present.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant
Each item present.

rules.title: Proportionate evidence by stage
rules.text: Outline: feasible strategy, space and levels, destination evidence, indicative storage. Full and reserved matters: complete detailed design. Conditions: exactly what the condition asks for.
rules.check: That missing detail is appropriate to the stage, not deferred without a feasible strategy.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant

rules.title: Recommend the national SuDS Strategy Template
rules.text: The EA templates (major and non-major) set out per-standard questions and evidence boxes. Completed templates make checking faster.
rules.check: Template sections against the evidence submitted.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant

rules.title: LLFA role
rules.text: Torbay is the Lead Local Flood Authority and statutory consultee for major development surface water drainage. For non-major development, the planning officer applies NPPF F8 and the Validation List with drainage advice as needed.
rules.check: Consultation route.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant
Consultation route.

rules.title: Other consents are separate
rules.text: Planning permission does not replace ordinary watercourse consent (Torbay, Land Drainage Act), EA flood risk activity permits, sewer connection approval, highway approval, environmental permits or landowner consent.
rules.when: Schemes affecting watercourses, sewers or highways.
rules.check: That consents are identified.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant
That consents are identified.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Non-mains foul drainage assessment
rules.text: Development using non-mains foul drainage needs a foul drainage assessment justifying why mains connection is not feasible.
rules.check: Assessment at validation.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant
Assessment at validation.
The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.

rules.title: Departures
rules.text: A national “shall” requirement needs an agreed departure to vary it; a “should” recommendation needs appropriate justification for an alternative. Where constraints prevent full compliance, maximise delivery and develop the justification in consultation with the approving body. A departure cannot override a prohibiting regulatory control. “Must” denotes a legislative or statutory obligation.
rules.check: The precise requirement, constraints, maximised delivery, reason, agreement and any overriding regulatory control.
evidence: Standards-compliance statement and indexed evidence register; Coordinated strategy, drawings, investigations and calculations; Condition-response and consent schedules where relevant

pages.title: Site and flood risk
pages.lede: Flood zones, the critical drainage area, flood risk assessment and the NPPF tests.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant What the evidence should show The site boundary, relevant present and future flood sources, coastal risk where applicable, and the development lifetime. How floor levels, safe access, residual risk and resilience relate to assessed flood conditions. The precise basis for each planning test, exemption, compatibility finding and CDA interpretation. Full evidence guide for this topic Annotated review examples Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Critical drainage area 2 checks FR-01 Check the critical drainage area boundary Officer guidance Use the Torbay CDA criteria for conservative screening across Torbay. For a site in Maidencombe, establish the current EA designation and boundary before relying on CDA status in a formal assessment. Applies when All development that could affect drainage. What to check The site against the current designation map, the applicable local policy and any written confirmation of the 2026 extension. Record the boundary and the basis of the assessment. Evidence to look for Dated designation map and recorded assessment basis Locate the application boundary and identify the source version. For Maidencombe, record the published source difference and the confirmation relied on. Gap to check A general statement that the whole borough is designated, without addressing the boundary evidence. Local interpretation Sources differ. The Local Plan (2015) and SFRA Level 1 (June 2026) say the whole of Torbay is a CDA. The Validation List (November 2024) and the draft SFRA Level 2A (June 2026) say Maidencombe is outside it. The EA national dataset published in September 2026 has a July 2025 geometry revision and does not establish the extension. Whole-Torbay screening is the working interpretation, not confirmation of a new formal boundary. The local Validation List still requires an FRA in Maidencombe. Sources Torbay evidence SFRA Level 1 CDA Local Plan Local Plan 6.5.2.15 Torbay CDA advice CDA Torbay validation Validation List 3.6.1 Torbay evidence (draft) SFRA Level 2A Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-02 Seek a contribution to wider flood risk reduction Torbay criterion Development in the CDA should be served by SuDS meeting the CDA criteria and should also contribute to a scheme that reduces risk for those liable to flood, for example by improving a constrained channel, culvert or bridge. Applies when New development in the CDA, proportionate to scale. What to check Whether the proposal identifies or contributes to a downstream improvement. ER1 allows a financial contribution to be requested. Evidence to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Torbay CDA advice CDA Local Plan Local Plan ER1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Flood risk assessment 4 checks FR-03 Require a flood risk assessment with a surface water drainage strategy Requirement A flood risk assessment (FRA), including a surface water drainage strategy, is a local validation requirement for householder, full, outline and reserved matters applications and relevant demolition in a conservation area. Applies when All listed application types anywhere in Torbay. For prior approvals, compare Validation List 4.1.4 and 4.2.15 and record the applicable planning class, submission scope and assessment basis. Their stated scopes differ; seek Council clarification where applicability is uncertain. What to check That an FRA is submitted before validation. Householder development in Flood Zone 1 can normally use the short Torbay proforma. Evidence to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Torbay validation Validation List 3.6.1 Torbay validation Validation List 4.1.4 Torbay validation Validation List 4.2.15 Torbay validation FRA forms Local Plan Local Plan ER1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-04 Require a site-specific FRA where NPPF F4 applies Requirement A site-specific FRA should accompany development proposals in Flood Zones 2, 3a and 3b. In Flood Zone 1, it should inform and accompany proposals on sites of 1 ha or more, land the EA has identified as having critical drainage problems, or land identified in an SFRA or the Flood Map for Planning as being at risk from any source now or in future. Applies when Any development meeting an F4 trigger. Confirm the current EA-designated boundary where that trigger is material; local FRA requirements also apply. What to check The F4 trigger and evidence, and an FRA proportionate to the scale, nature and location of the development, covering relevant flood sources, future climate and lifetime. Evidence to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment Identify the F4 trigger from the flood zone, site area, EA designation or SFRA/Flood Map evidence. Trace relevant flood sources, future conditions and lifetime through the proportionate assessment. Gap to check A single Flood Zone image or an assessment that omits the relevant source or trigger. Sources National policy NPPF F4 Environment Agency Flood map for planning Torbay evidence Surface water map (current) Torbay evidence Surface water map (future) Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-05 Check the Local Plan FRA level Torbay criterion A basic FRA for all development; a more detailed FRA for Flood Zone 1 sites of 1 ha or more (including those draining into Flood Zones 2 and 3), all new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3, and development near seafronts at risk from wave action. Applies when All development. What to check That the depth of the FRA matches the ER1 category. Evidence to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Local Plan Local Plan ER1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-12 Use the 2026 SFRA maps Officer guidance Check the SFRA surface water maps (current and future) and the Flood Zone 3b map, alongside the EA Flood map for planning. Applies when All site assessments. What to check That the FRA uses the current SFRA mapping, not superseded 2008 or 2010 data. Evidence to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Torbay evidence Surface water map (current) Torbay evidence Surface water map (future) Torbay evidence Flood Zone 3b map Environment Agency Flood map for planning Torbay evidence flood reports Topic evidence guide Link to this check NPPF tests 6 checks FR-06 Apply the sequential test Conditional Steer development to the lowest flood risk land where suitable alternative sites are reasonably available. Torbay's Validation List includes a flooding sequential test for new dwellings in Flood Zones 2 and 3. Check the current national exemptions and the applicable local requirements. Applies when Development at risk now or in future from any source, unless an exemption in NPPF F5.2 is demonstrated. What to check That the sequential test is passed or the precise F5.2 exemption is supported by evidence. The test area should not exceed the anticipated catchment of the development's occupiers or users. Evidence to look for Sequential-test evidence or precise exemption Match the proposal and FRA to the relevant F5.2 exemption, or demonstrate the sequential test using suitable reasonably available alternatives and the appropriate catchment. Gap to check An obsolete change-of-use exemption or an unsupported assertion that the site is exempt. F5.2 exempts allocated sites tested during plan preparation; sites where an FRA clearly demonstrates that no built development, access or escape routes, land raising or other vulnerable elements are on land at risk now or in future; or surface-water-only risk where layout, design and mitigation meet F7 lifetime safety without increasing risk elsewhere. It also exempts householder development, non-residential extensions with a footprint less than 250 m², and changes of use other than to caravan, camping, chalet, mobile home or park home sites. Sources National policy NPPF F5 Torbay validation Validation List 3.6.2 Local Plan Local Plan ER1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-07 Check flood-zone compatibility and the exception test Conditional Check the use against NPPF Annex F tables 2 and 3: incompatible development should be refused. Where the exception test applies, demonstrate wider sustainability benefits that outweigh flood risk, lifetime safety under F7, and no increase in flood risk elsewhere with an overall reduction where possible. Applies when Development in Flood Zones 2, 3a or 3b; the exception-test requirement depends on vulnerability and the exemptions in NPPF F6.2. What to check Flood-zone and vulnerability classification, compatibility, all three exception-test criteria supported by the FRA, or the evidenced F6.2 exemption. Evidence to look for Flood-zone compatibility and exception-test evidence Check Annex F classification and compatibility first, then all three F6.1 criteria or the precise F6.2 exception-test exemption. Gap to check A passed exception test used to justify an incompatible use, or a missing lifetime-safety or off-site-risk criterion. F6.2 removes the exception-test requirement for forms or circumstances exempt from the sequential test under F5, and for allocated sites tested at plan-making stage unless flood risk has since significantly increased or the proposal has changed significantly to introduce a more vulnerable use. This does not remove the separate flood-zone compatibility check. Sources National policy NPPF F6 National policy NPPF F5 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-08 Make development safe from flooding Requirement Development should not present a flood risk to occupiers, users or visitors or increase flood risk elsewhere. Where risk exists now or in future, locate the most vulnerable development in the lowest risk areas unless overriding reasons justify otherwise. Demonstrate lifetime safety for its users, safe management of residual risk and, where appropriate, safe access and escape as part of an agreed emergency plan. Provide flood resistance and resilience allowing rapid return to use without significant refurbishment. Applies when All development at risk of flooding now or in future. What to check Siting and any overriding reasons, lifetime safety, finished floor levels, residual risk, the applicable emergency plan and access arrangements, resilience and effects elsewhere. Evidence to look for Lifetime safety, residual-risk and resilience evidence Relate the layout, any overriding siting reasons, user vulnerability, applicable emergency plan, access, resilience and effects elsewhere to the assessed present and future flood conditions. Gap to check Safe access asserted without the relevant emergency arrangements, or resilience described without an effective return-to-use outcome. Sources National policy NPPF F7 Local Plan Local Plan ER1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-09 Set finished floor levels above the design flood level Torbay criterion Set finished floor levels above the 1 in 100 year flood level, with climate change, where the site is at risk. Applies when Sites at risk of flooding. What to check Floor levels against modelled flood levels. Evidence to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Torbay evidence SFRA Level 1 7.8 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-10 Coastal change and future tidal inundation Conditional NPPF F9 covers coastal change management areas and other areas likely to face coastal erosion or tidal inundation over the next century. Demonstrate lifetime safety, consistency with the relevant Shoreline Management Plan without unacceptable effects on coastal change processes, and wider sustainability benefits that justify development. Torbay's Validation List requires a coastal change vulnerability assessment within a coastal change management area. Applies when Sites within a coastal change management area or other areas within the national F9 risk scope. What to check The national coastal-erosion map and current local evidence, all F9 criteria, any applicable local vulnerability-assessment requirement and drainage effects on coastal stability. Evidence to look for Coastal-risk scope and assessment evidence Check mapped coastal change management areas and the wider national F9 coastal-erosion or tidal-inundation scope. Demonstrate all F9 criteria and the local validation assessment where its trigger applies. Gap to check A site outside a mapped coastal change management area treated as automatically outside national F9. Sources National policy NPPF F9 Torbay validation Validation List 3.1.15 Local Plan Local Plan C3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FR-11 No basement accommodation where there is danger of inundation Requirement Basement accommodation, including changes of use or basement parking, will not be permitted where there is danger of inundation and risk to life. Applies when Proposals with basements in areas at risk. What to check Basement flood risk in the FRA. Evidence to look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts; Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan; Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Local Plan Local Plan ER1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Where water goes
pages.lede: The five-step destination hierarchy, discharge agreements, foul separation and pumping. National standard 1.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights What the evidence should show How each higher destination is used as far as practicable and why a lower destination is needed. Where each area drains and whether a gravity connection is deliverable. The proposed connection, receiving capacity, rates, volumes and necessary lifetime rights. Full evidence guide for this topic Annotated review examples Match the document, revision and page to each check below. The hierarchy 4 checks RD-01 Follow the destination hierarchy Requirement Discharge runoff to the following destinations, to the maximum extent practicable, in this order: 1 collect for non-potable use; 2 infiltrate to ground; 3 discharge to an above-ground surface water body; 4 discharge to a surface water sewer or other piped surface water system; 5 discharge to a combined sewer. Applies when All development. What to check That each higher destination has been assessed and used as far as practicable. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. The Local Plan (2015) and the Torbay guide (2022) start the hierarchy at infiltration. The national standards (2025) put reuse first. Reuse first is the current national position in standard 1.2. Sources National standard 1.2 Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 1.0 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-02 Evidence for using a lower destination Requirement Evidence shall show all higher priority destinations have been used to the maximum extent practicable. Higher cost alone is not a reason to use a lower destination. Applies when Any use of destinations 2 to 5. What to check Site evidence (tests, levels, distances), not assertion or cost alone. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal For each higher destination, identify the site evidence, practicable use and reason any remaining runoff needs a lower destination. Gap to check A conclusion that infiltration is unsuitable without the supporting assessment. Sources National standard 1.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-03 Maximise each destination in order Requirement Where more than one destination is used, maximise each one's ability to accept runoff in order of priority. Applies when Split-destination designs. What to check The proportion of area to each destination. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.
