Sources National standard 1.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-17 Ask for a fallback destination Recommendation Ask for a fallback (Plan B) destination if infiltration proves unsuitable at detailed design or a connection is refused. Applies when Outline and full applications relying on infiltration or an unconfirmed connection. What to check A deliverable fallback that still meets the discharge limits. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Environment Agency EA SuDS templates Topic evidence guide Link to this check General requirements 5 checks RD-04 Contamination is not an automatic reason to move down Requirement Do not discount higher priority destinations because a site is or was contaminated where practicable remediation can be designed with the drainage. Applies when Brownfield or contaminated sites. What to check That remediation and drainage options were considered together. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.5 Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-05 Secure rights over third-party land Requirement Where discharge needs third-party land, provide evidence of easements for the lifetime of the development. Applies when Outfalls or routes across land not owned by the applicant. What to check Easement or agreement evidence. Where rights cannot be obtained, the council may have powers under FWMA 2010 Schedule 2 paragraph 29(1). Evidence to look for Land-rights evidence and route plan Match the proposed connection and access route to the land affected and the rights needed for construction, use and maintenance. Gap to check A drainage line crossing third-party land with no evidence of the necessary rights. Sources National standard 1.6 National standard 1.6.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-06 No increase in flood risk elsewhere Requirement Runoff from the development shall not increase flood risk elsewhere from any source. Applies when All development. What to check Downstream effects, adjacent land and the receiving system. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.7 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Local Plan Local Plan ER1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-07 No depletion of waters Requirement The design shall not deplete surface waters or groundwater beyond safe environmental levels. Applies when Schemes that divert runoff away from its natural catchment or receiving water. What to check That natural catchments are replicated as far as practicable. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.9 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-08 Keep surface water out of foul sewers Requirement Essentially uncontaminated surface water shall not discharge to a foul-only sewer. The national standards except runoff integral to a foul pumping station. Very contaminated runoff is dealt with separately under the water quality requirements, including any consent for foul discharge. Applies when All development. What to check The runoff type, sewer classification, connection drawings and any consent for the exceptional discharge. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.10 National standard 4.8 National standard 4.9 Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Reuse 2 checks RD-09 Consider rainwater harvesting Conditional Rainwater harvesting shall be considered where there is a non-potable demand with enough catchment, a need for landscape irrigation, or the area is seriously water stressed. Applies when Any of the three triggers applies. Examples include industrial, commercial, educational, public sector, residential and multiple-occupancy buildings. What to check A reasoned demand assessment. If harvesting is not used, the reason. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.11 Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-10 Design rainwater harvesting for its intended use Conditional Harvesting used to manage large rainfall events shall be designed to BS EN 16941. Harvesting design shall follow best practice and demonstrate effectiveness against a rainfall time series. Communal systems outside the curtilage shall consider public health and security. Applies when Rainwater harvesting is proposed; apply the large-event and communal-system conditions where relevant. What to check Rainfall time series, demand profile, applicable design standard and public health and security assessment. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.12 National standard 1.13 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Agreements 4 checks RD-11 Agree discharge to a watercourse in writing Conditional The principle of discharge to an above-ground water body, including rates and volumes, shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authority. This does not replace permits or consents. Applies when Destination 3. What to check Written agreement in principle; ordinary watercourse consent or EA permit as needed. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.19 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Torbay consent Watercourse consent Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-12 Agree sewer connections in writing with capacity Conditional Discharge to a surface water sewer, other piped drainage or combined sewer shall be agreed in writing with the relevant risk management authorities and the downstream owner if different. Include rates, volumes, connection location and confirmation of capacity. Applies when Destinations 4 and 5. What to check Written agreements from the relevant authorities and owner; capacity evidence and the proposed connection point. Evidence to look for Written connection and capacity evidence Check the receiving system, location, proposed discharge and the agreed capacity basis against the submitted design. Gap to check An enquiry acknowledgement or a sewer-location plan used as connection approval. Sources National standard 1.20 National standard 1.22 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Sewerage undertaker South West Water Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-13 Combined sewer: control to greenfield and assess pollution Conditional A combined sewer is the last destination in the hierarchy. ER2 requires greenfield discharge rates. Assess pollution from surcharge or flooding of the receiving combined sewer and provide mitigation demonstrating that pollution risk is not increased. Where capacity is insufficient, the developer should work with the undertaker to fund capacity. Applies when Destination 5. What to check Hierarchy evidence, greenfield rate, receiving sewer capacity, pollution assessment and effective mitigation. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.21 National standard 1.22.1 National standard 1.23 Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-14 Torquay: appropriate assessment where the hierarchy is not met Conditional In Torquay, development that has not met the ER2 drainage hierarchy will be subject to an individual Habitats Regulations Appropriate Assessment. Applies when Torquay sites that do not meet the hierarchy. What to check Refer to the council ecologist. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Pumping 2 checks RD-15 Pumping by exception only Conditional Pumping shall be by exception and agreed with the approving body. Assess pumping against a lower destination reachable by gravity, including cost, failure risk, pollution and flooding. Pump only the parts that cannot drain by gravity. Applies when Any pumped surface water. What to check The gravity alternative, the area pumped and the failure assessment. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.24 National standard 1.25 National standard 1.26 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-16 Pumping station design and downstream capacity Conditional Design pumping stations to recognised guidance unless an alternative is agreed in writing with the proposed adoption organisation and the approving body if different. Where a downstream pumping station receives the flow, provide written confirmation of capacity from its owner. Applies when Pumped systems or downstream pumping stations. What to check Design standard and owner capacity letter. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.27 National standard 1.28 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Infiltration and groundwater
pages.lede: Testing, groundwater separation, factors of safety, half-drain time and ground stability.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Located investigation and test records Groundwater and geotechnical evidence Feature sections and infiltration calculations What the evidence should show Tests representative of the proposed feature locations and depths, with a traceable design rate. Feature base and maximum likely groundwater on a common level datum. The adopted safety factor, half-drain performance, stability and pollution assessment. Full evidence guide for this topic Follow the decision guide Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Testing 2 checks IG-01 Prove infiltration with site testing Requirement Infiltration depends on suitable ground and adequate tested rates. Geotechnical investigation shall confirm the ground is suitable using recognised methods. Mapping can form an initial evidence base. Applies when Infiltration proposed, or evidence needed to assess its feasibility. Mapping can inform whether ground investigation is necessary. What to check Adequate site evidence for the hierarchy decision; location-specific investigation and testing where infiltration is relied on. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.14 National standard 1.14.1 National standard 3.14 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-02 Test to BRE 365 at the feature location and depth Torbay criterion Test in strict accordance with BRE 365 at the location and depth of each feature (or within 20 m where results are similar). Three consecutive tests to near emptying; extrapolation from 25% effective depth is not accepted. Permeable paving tested at 20 m intervals with pits at least 1.5 m × 1 m. Applies when All infiltration designs. What to check Test locations against the layout; three fills; full drainage. Evidence to look for Test plan and test records Match test locations, depths, logs and adopted infiltration rate to the proposed feature. Read the Torbay test criterion alongside the detailed ground evidence. Gap to check Unlocated test results or a test depth unrelated to the feature base. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Groundwater 2 checks IG-03 Keep 1 m above maximum groundwater Requirement The base of infiltration features shall be at least 1 m above the maximum likely groundwater level. For systems wholly relying on infiltration this 1 m unsaturated zone also protects groundwater. Applies when All infiltration. What to check Base level against groundwater evidence. Evidence to look for Groundwater evidence and feature section Show maximum likely groundwater and the proposed base on the same datum, with the separation demonstrated. Gap to check Groundwater depth quoted without relating it to the feature base. Sources National standard 1.15 National standard 4.16.1 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-04 Establish wet-winter groundwater levels Recommendation Confirm groundwater levels through investigation during high groundwater periods, using records at or near the site, with enough data to show seasonal levels. Applies when Infiltration designs. What to check Monitoring period and season. Single dry-season readings are not enough. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. There is no Torbay rule for the monitoring period. Devon asks for monitoring over November to May (reference only). Sources National standard 3.11 National standard 4.16.2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Ground risks 6 checks IG-05 No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding Requirement Infiltration shall not cause unacceptable instability or subsidence (including riverbanks and coastal features), groundwater or surface water pollution, groundwater flooding, or ingress to foul or combined sewers. Applies when All infiltration. What to check Ground risk assessment. Torbay guide 4.2 lists slopes over 10%, unstable or contaminated ground, services and proximity. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.16 National standard 1.17 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-06 Deep-bore infiltration by exception Conditional Deep-bore infiltration is not a SuDS approach. It shall be by exception with an agreement in principle from the relevant risk management authority. Applies when Deep-bore soakaways or boreholes. What to check Exceptional justification and EA agreement or permit. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.18 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-10 Assess point infiltration within 5 m of structures Requirement Where runoff goes to point infiltration within 5 m of existing or proposed buildings, roads, embankments or other infrastructure, assess instability and mitigate. Unstable geology may need more than 5 m. Applies when Soakaways within 5 m. What to check Distances on the layout and the stability assessment. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.27 National standard 7.27.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-11 Assess diffuse infiltration within 3 m of buildings Requirement Diffuse near-surface infiltration taking direct rainfall or a very small catchment similar in area to the infiltration surface should not normally pose a structural risk. Such proposals within 3 m of a building shall be assessed and mitigated where required. This reassurance does not extend to large contributing catchments. Applies when Permeable surfaces or similar within 3 m of a building. What to check Distance, contributing area relative to the infiltration surface, ground conditions, structural risk and any mitigation. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.27.2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-13 Groundwater protection and contaminated land Requirement Follow EA groundwater protection guidance when discharging to ground. Infiltration through contaminated land is allowed only where there is no risk of mobilising pollutants. Applies when Infiltration, especially on brownfield land or in source protection zones. What to check Groundwater risk assessment. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.15 National standard 4.16 National standard 4.17 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-14 Structural loading below trafficked surfaces Recommendation Where infiltration lies beneath trafficked surfaces, consider structural loading and soil weakening when saturated. Applies when Infiltration under roads or parking. What to check Structural design note. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.26 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Hydraulic design 4 checks IG-07 Do not rely only on point infiltration below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s Requirement Point infiltration (for example soakaways) shall not be fully relied on where infiltration rates are below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s. Applies when Soakaways and other point features. What to check Tested rate. If lower, an additional destination. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.15 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-08 Half-empty within 24 hours Requirement Infiltration features shall half-empty their runoff volume within 24 hours for events up to the 3.3% AEP event. Applies when All infiltration features. What to check Half-drain time in the calculations. Evidence to look for Infiltration storage and half-drain calculation Identify the tested rate, storage geometry and safety factor used to demonstrate the stated half-drain performance. Gap to check A storage-volume result without a drain-time check. Sources National standard 3.16 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-09 Use the Torbay factor of safety Torbay criterion Size infiltration with the RP156 factor of safety. Torbay expects the 'minor damage to external areas or inconvenience' values: 2 for areas under 100 m², 3 for 100 to 1000 m², 5 for over 1000 m². Use 10 where failure would damage buildings or cause major inconvenience. Applies when Infiltration designed with the RP156 (CIRIA) method. What to check Factor used against drained area and consequence. Evidence to look for Calculation input and consequence assessment Trace the RP156 factor to the drained area and consequence of failure, and check it is applied in the calculation. Gap to check A factor stated in the narrative but absent or different in the calculation. Sources National standard 3.17 National standard National standards, table S3.1 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-12 Protect infiltration surfaces from clogging Recommendation Features that infiltrate should include or be preceded by pre-treatment that protects the infiltration surface. Applies when All infiltration. What to check Silt traps, filter strips or other pre-treatment. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.13 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Everyday rainfall
pages.lede: Interception of the first 5 mm, deemed-compliant features and area ratios. National standard 2.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement What the evidence should show How runoff from each positively drained surface is retained, used or lost within the development. The actual contributing and receiving areas, lining, levels, gradient and outlet arrangement. Every condition supporting a feature-specific presumption, including relevant infiltration evidence. Full evidence guide for this topic Annotated review examples Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Target 2 checks ER-01 Intercept the first 5 mm Requirement Deliver interception within the development so the first 5 mm of rainfall produces no runoff for at least 80% of summer events (May to October) and 50% of winter events (November to April). Applies when All development. What to check Interception method for every positively drained surface. Evidence to look for Surface-by-surface interception schedule Identify each positively drained surface, its receiving feature, the loss or reuse mechanism and the evidence supporting it. Gap to check One site-wide assertion that all SuDS provide interception. Sources National standard 2.1 National standard 2.5 National standard 2.6 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-02 Design interception with quality, amenity and biodiversity Requirement Show the everyday rainfall approach was developed alongside water quality, amenity and biodiversity. Applies when All development. What to check That interception features are part of the landscape and treatment train. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 2.2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Deemed compliance 3 checks ER-03 Deemed compliance: harvesting Conditional Optional deemed-compliance route: a development is deemed compliant if rainwater harvesting means no runoff leaves the development for lower-order events, shown by BS EN 16941 calculations. This does not require the feature to be provided. Applies when Harvesting serves all relevant areas. What to check BS EN 16941 calculations. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 2.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-04 Deemed compliance: full infiltration of monthly events Conditional Optional deemed-compliance route: a development is deemed compliant if it infiltrates entirely to ground so no runoff leaves for events with a 1 in 1 or greater chance each month, shown by calculations and infiltration tests. A soakaway designed for 1 in 1 or 1 in 10 year events already meets this. This does not require the feature to be provided. Applies when Fully infiltrating sites. What to check Infiltration calculations and tests. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 2.4 Environment Agency EA SuDS templates Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-05 Simplified approach needs agreement Conditional Where no modelling is used, the simplified approach (features and ratios in 2.7) may be accepted with the approving body's agreement. Where a feature lacks capacity, downstream features can add it, with detailed calculations. Applies when Interception shown without modelling. What to check That 2.7 presumptions are met exactly. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 2.6.2 National standard 2.6.3 National standard 2.6.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Feature ratios 8 checks ER-06 Green roofs and walls Conditional Surfaces with green roofs or walls that drain only their own area comply. Applies when Green roofs or walls. What to check That no other area drains onto the roof. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-07 Rainwater harvesting and water butts Conditional Surfaces draining to BS EN 16941 harvesting based on regular daily non-potable demand comply. Water butts limited to garden use in dry periods do not. Applies when Harvesting or water butts. What to check Daily demand basis; water butts not counted unless designed with calculations. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-08 Permeable surfaces Conditional No added area: complies (lined or unlined). Unlined with added impermeable area no greater than the permeable area: complies. Unlined over ground above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 5× the permeable area may be added (100 m² impermeable needs 20 m² permeable). Lined with added area: does not comply; add downstream interception. Applies when Permeable paving. What to check Lining, added area ratio and tested rate. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-09 Swales Conditional Fall under 1:100 with at least 500 mm suitable base: up to 5× the vegetated base area. Unlined, fall under 1:100 and over 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 25×. Steeper than 1:100: no interception unless shown by design. Areas draining within 5 m of an unlined swale outlet do not count unless the swale is flat with a raised outlet. Applies when Swales. What to check Long-section fall, base material, lining and outlet arrangement. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-10 Infiltration trenches and soakaways Conditional Roads drained by infiltration trenches comply. Areas drained to systems designed to infiltrate 1-in-1-month events comply. Applies when Trenches and soakaways. What to check Design event for the infiltration system. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-11 Detention basins Conditional A flat, unlined vegetated basin base below the outlet, without specific provision routing low flows directly to the outlet, can receive up to five times that base area. Above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s infiltration, the ratio can be up to 25:1. Higher ratios need justification using below-outlet storage, higher infiltration rates and detailed design. Provide upstream sediment control for infiltrating basins. Applies when Detention basins. What to check Effective below-outlet base area, lining, levels, low-flow routing, tested infiltration and sediment control; calculations for a higher ratio. Evidence to look for Basin catchment plan and section Identify effective receiving area, lining, infiltration, low-flow route and levels below the outlet. Test every applicable basin condition. Gap to check An area ratio alone, or storage above the outlet used to prove interception. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-12 Bioretention and rain gardens Conditional Unlined bioretention complies where the impermeable area is up to 5× the vegetated surface receiving runoff (100 m² needs 20 m²). Applies when Rain gardens, bioretention, tree pits designed as bioretention. What to check Unlined; area ratio. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-13 Attenuation ponds give no interception Conditional Areas drained by attenuation ponds with a permanent pool are assumed not to deliver interception. Applies when Wet ponds. What to check Interception provided upstream instead. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Runoff rates, volumes and storage
pages.lede: Greenfield rates, Torbay discharge limits, climate change, urban creep and storage. National standard 3.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary What the evidence should show Which national branch applies, using developed volume discharged to surface waters or sewers compared with greenfield runoff for the same 1% AEP, six-hour event. Applicable local limits shown separately, with their geographical and policy basis. Lifetime, climate allowance, urban creep, rainfall and duration assumptions reconciled with the drawings. Full evidence guide for this topic Follow the decision guide Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Discharge limits 8 checks RV-01 Control rate and volume for the 1% and 50% events Requirement When discharging to a water body or sewer, control the 1% AEP runoff (rate and volume) so flood risk elsewhere does not increase, and the 50% AEP rate so it has no negative impact. Size infiltration for the design event. Applies when All positive discharges. What to check Event table showing 50%, 3.3% and 1% AEP rates. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.2 National standard 3.3 National standard 3.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-02 CDA: mimic greenfield, capped at the 1 in 10 year rate Torbay criterion All off-site discharges should mimic greenfield performance up to a maximum of the 1 in 10 year greenfield rate. Where infiltration is not suitable, limit flows to the 1 in 10 year greenfield rate. Applies when Positive discharges subject to Torbay CDA criteria and applicable local planning policy. What to check Event-specific greenfield performance and the Q10 ceiling; record the site and policy basis. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Torbay CDA advice CDA Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Local Plan Local Plan 6.5.2.15 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-03 50% AEP limit Requirement Limit the 50% AEP peak to the 50% AEP greenfield rate (Qbar or Qmed) or 3 l/s/ha, whichever is greater. Applies when Discharge to surface waters or sewers. What to check Qbar calculation and the allowable rate. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.18 National standard 3.27 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-04 1% AEP limit: volume test Requirement Compare the volume discharged to surface waters or sewers in the developed 1% AEP 6-hour event with greenfield runoff volume for the same event. If greater, limit the 1% AEP peak to max(the 50% AEP greenfield rate, 3 l/s/ha). If equal or less, limit it to max(the 1% AEP greenfield rate, 3 l/s/ha). Distinguish runoff generated from the volume remaining to be discharged after interception, reuse or infiltration. Applies when Discharge to surface waters or sewers. What to check The 6-hour discharged-volume comparison, its contributing area and the national branch used. Evidence to look for Greenfield runoff and developed discharged-volume comparison Compare the same 1% AEP, six-hour event and contributing area. Identify the developed volume discharged to surface waters or sewers after interception, reuse or infiltration, then select the correct national discharge-limit branch. Gap to check Peak rates alone, or generated runoff used without identifying the volume discharged to surface waters or sewers. Sources National standard 3.19 National standard 3.20 National standard 3.28 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-05 Compare the applicable national and local limits Officer guidance Calculate the national 50% AEP limit and the correct 1% AEP volume branch. Separately show the applicable local greenfield performance and Q10 ceiling. Use the more stringent applicable criterion for each event where the evidence-based local approach satisfies national standard 3.10. Do not raise a calculated limit automatically to 1.5 l/s. Applies when Positive discharges where national and local criteria overlap. What to check Use the runoff comparison; record the local policy basis, the governing event and any agreed departure. Evidence to look for National and local event comparison Show each applicable limit, its event, site scope and policy basis. Record how a source difference or agreement affects the chosen criterion. Gap to check One blended discharge limit with no explanation of the national and local tests. Local interpretation National 3.10 gives a more stringent, evidence-based local approach precedence. Torbay guide 3.5 says the CDA criteria take preference where they overlap. The CDA's 'mimic greenfield' has no 3 l/s/ha floor, so for small or low-runoff sites it is stricter than national 3.18. Sources National standard 3.10 Torbay CDA advice CDA Torbay guidance SuDS guide 3.5 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-06 Check proposals relying on the published 1.5 l/s minimum Torbay criterion The September 2022 Torbay guide states a minimum positive discharge of 1.5 l/s. Where that exceeds a current national or applicable local limit, record the conflict and obtain the approving body's agreement to the proposed approach. Applies when A proposal relies on 1.5 l/s despite a lower calculated limit. What to check The lower calculated limit, evidence for the proposed control, blockage protection and the recorded approval or departure. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Local interpretation This published local minimum is not a national exemption. It can conflict with low greenfield rates on sites of different sizes. The comparison tool leaves the conflict visible. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-07 Brownfield sites: check the greenfield expectation Torbay criterion Torbay CDA advice and the published local guide expect brownfield runoff to meet greenfield criteria. National standard 3.21 permits an evidenced, agreed relaxation in defined circumstances, capped by 3.21.1. Do not assume that route overrides a more stringent applicable local approach. Applies when Previously developed sites. What to check Greenfield rates used, not existing rates. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Local interpretation National 3.21 allows a relaxation of up to 5× greenfield with evidence and agreement. The CDA and Torbay guide require brownfield to match greenfield, so assess whether the local approach takes precedence under national 3.10. Record the applicable geographic and policy basis and any requested departure. Sources Torbay CDA advice CDA Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Local Plan Local Plan 6.5.2.15 National standard 3.21 National standard 3.21.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-08 Tidal or sea outfalls Conditional Where runoff goes to a water body that can take uncontrolled discharge without environmental impact (the sea, large tidal estuaries), 3.3 and 3.4 may not apply, subject to written approval from the relevant risk management authority. Applies when Direct discharge to the sea or a large tidal estuary. What to check Written approval; erosion, tide locking, water quality and ecology. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.9 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Greenfield runoff 1 check RV-09 Greenfield runoff method Requirement Estimate greenfield rates with the EA Flood Estimation Guidelines, using the whole area that could drain to the system (permeable and impermeable), with soil parameters confirmed by ground investigation. Recommendation (3.30): calculate baseline greenfield rates and volumes without a climate change allowance. Applies when All greenfield calculations. What to check Method, area used, SOIL/HOST class evidence. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.26 National standard 3.29 National standard 3.30 National standard 3.31 Environment Agency Flood Estimation Guidelines Topic evidence guide Link to this check Design inputs 3 checks RV-10 Climate change: upper end allowance Requirement Use the latest EA allowances, upper end, for the epoch matching the design life. Torbay (South Devon catchment), 2070s epoch (2061 to 2125): +40% for 3.3% AEP and +50% for 1% AEP. 2050s epoch (2022 to 2060): +35% and +45%. Record the development's lifetime and how it is covered by the selected epoch. Applies when 3.3% and 1% AEP design events. What to check Allowance and epoch against the design life. Evidence to look for Lifetime and climate input schedule Match catchment, development lifetime, epoch and upper-end allowance to the source and hydraulic model inputs. Gap to check A percentage copied from an older report without checking the lifetime and current source. Local interpretation National SuDS standard 3.8 specifies the upper-end allowance for drainage design. EA general surface-water FRA guidance separately describes central allowances for shorter lifetimes; do not substitute those for the national SuDS design requirement. The Torbay guide's 50% matches the 2070s upper end for the 1% event. For a shorter-lifetime proposal where the current national allowance is lower, record how the published local 50% criterion is applied and obtain agreement for the assessment basis. Sources National standard 3.8 Environment Agency EA allowances Environment Agency EA allowance guidance Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-11 Urban creep: 10% on the proposed impermeable area Torbay criterion Add 10% to the impermeable area of the proposed development in the calculations. Applies when Applications after 1 October 2022. What to check Impermeable area × 1.10 in the model. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Local interpretation National 3.33 applies 10% to impermeable area within property curtilages, and 0% for flats without private permeable space. Torbay's published expectation covers the whole proposed impermeable area. Show both scopes where they differ. Record the model areas, assessment basis and any council agreement; approval of a blanket reconciliation is not recorded. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 3.11 National standard 3.33 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-12 Latest rainfall data and runoff method Requirement Use the latest rainfall data (FEH22). Recommendation (3.32): follow industry practice for runoff coefficients; do not ignore contributing pervious surfaces or SuDS footprints. Applies when All hydraulic calculations. What to check Rainfall dataset and runoff parameters. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.34 National standard 3.32 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Storage 5 checks RV-13 Use the critical duration Recommendation Use the critical duration storm to set maximum water levels, flows and storage. Different features may have different critical durations. Applies when All storage design. What to check Range of durations modelled. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.23 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-14 Model the SuDS and pipes together Torbay criterion Represent the SuDS features and the connecting pipe network as one model. Applies when Full, reserved matters and conditions. What to check One network model matching the layout drawings. Evidence to look for Coordinated model and drainage drawings Reconcile catchments, feature storage, pipe and control levels, outlet conditions and interactions across the complete system. Gap to check Separate calculations that overlook interaction between the features and pipes. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 5.0 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-15 Attenuate at several points Recommendation Attenuate at multiple points across the development rather than one feature at the outfall, unless justified. Applies when All development with storage. What to check Distribution of storage. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.12 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-16 Protect small flow controls Requirement Where the allowable rate needs an orifice (or equivalent) under 50 mm, protect it robustly from blockage. Assess blockage risk for all controls. Applies when All flow controls. What to check Control diameter and protection detail. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.22 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RV-17 Non-technical summary Requirement Provide detailed non-technical summaries of the design approach, calculations, results and conclusions. Applies when Full, reserved matters, conditions. What to check Summary matches the calculations. Evidence to look for Greenfield calculation and contributing-area schedule; Coordinated hydraulic model and input schedule; Event results, volume comparison and non-technical summary Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.25 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Flooding and exceedance
pages.lede: Design event performance, freeboard, blockage, surcharge and exceedance routes. National standard 3.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections Event results identifying flooded and protected locations Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments What the evidence should show Where water moves when capacity is exceeded and the consequences at site boundaries. The relationship between water levels, buildings, vulnerable plant and escape routes. The effects of incoming runoff, submerged outfalls, blockage and justified freeboard. Full evidence guide for this topic Annotated review examples Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Design events 6 checks FE-01 No flooding up to 3.3% AEP plus climate change Requirement No flooding on any part of the site up to the 3.3% AEP (1 in 30 year) event plus climate change, unless the area is designed to hold or convey water. Applies when All development. What to check Model results for the 3.3% AEP + cc event. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.35 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-02 Protect buildings, plant and escape routes up to 1% AEP plus climate change Requirement No flooding of buildings (including basements), utility plant susceptible to water, or safe access and escape routes up to the 1% AEP event plus climate change. Manage any system flooding within the development. Applies when All development. What to check Flood volumes and locations for 1% AEP + cc against levels. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.36 National standard 3.5 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-03 Below-ground storage: suggested modelling approaches Recommendation Where there is no above-ground storage, Torbay suggests either: 1) 1% AEP + cc with top water level below the incoming pipe invert; or 2) 1% AEP with no flooding, and 3.3% AEP + cc top water level below the incoming pipe invert. Applies when Systems with only below-ground storage. What to check Top water level against incoming invert. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. These are suggested modelling approaches. They do not replace the applicable national climate-adjusted performance, flooding and protected-receptor checks in FE-01 and FE-02. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-04 Provide freeboard Requirement Provide freeboard to buildings, vulnerable plant and escape routes, reflecting uncertainty and the consequence of flooding. Applies when All development. What to check Levels and freeboard justification. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.37 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-05 Temporary flooding of shared spaces and roads Requirement Assess temporary flooding of multifunctional areas for risk, impact and recovery. Any flooding of highways shall be shallow, slow and low hazard and not affect escape routes. Applies when Designs that store water on open space or roads. What to check Depths, velocities and routes. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.38 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-08 Keep features out of the 1% AEP flood area Requirement Do not place drainage features in areas at risk in the 1% AEP pluvial or fluvial event unless designed to operate in flood conditions. Applies when Sites with mapped flood risk. What to check Feature locations against SFRA and EA mapping. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.13 Torbay evidence Surface water map (current) Topic evidence guide Link to this check Off-site flows 2 checks FE-06 Flows from adjacent land Requirement Account for runoff from adjacent sites onto the development. Convey it safely; no attenuation needed unless it interacts with the system. Off-site flooding up to 1% AEP should be managed or safely routed without increasing downstream risk. Applies when Sites receiving overland flow. What to check Upslope catchment and routing plan. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.39 National standard 3.39.1 National standard 3.6 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-07 Surcharged outfalls and flood-locking Requirement Analyse the effect of a surcharged outfall and flood-locking (watercourse, sea, estuary or groundwater levels), adding storage if needed. Applies when Outfalls that may be submerged or surcharged. What to check Model run with surcharged outfall. Evidence to look for Outfall boundary and surcharge assessment Compare relevant normal and surcharged conditions, showing changes to stored volume, water levels and protected locations. Gap to check A free-discharge model where the receiving system could surcharge or flood-lock. Sources National standard 3.24 National standard 3.39.2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Exceedance and blockage 2 checks FE-09 Exceedance routes Requirement Assess events beyond 1% AEP and show exceedance routes on a plan, with no adverse risk to the development or elsewhere. Applies when All development. What to check Exceedance plan with levels. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan Follow each route past buildings and access routes to its destination. Check incoming flows and boundary consequences. Gap to check Arrows showing direction but no levels, destination or effects on neighbouring land. Sources National standard 3.40 National standard 3.7 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.5 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-10 Investigate blockage Torbay criterion Investigate the effect of blockages on the system and show the resulting flood routes. Applies when All development. What to check Blockage scenario on the exceedance plan. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.5 National standard 7.16 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Water quality
pages.lede: Pollution hazard, management train, spills, groundwater protection and outfalls. National standard 4.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details What the evidence should show The pollution hazard, receptor sensitivity and treatment appropriate to each contributing area. How the successive measures manage pollutants over the design life. How a spill can be isolated, removed and the system restored; infiltration risks assessed separately. Full evidence guide for this topic Annotated review examples Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Risk and treatment 7 checks WQ-01 Base the treatment on a risk assessment Requirement Base the management train on a water quality risk assessment matched to the pollution hazard and receiving water sensitivity. Use the Simple Index Approach (C753) or another agreed method. Applies when All development. What to check Hazard level, sensitivity and treatment indices. Evidence to look for Pollution-risk and treatment assessment Trace land use, receptor sensitivity and pollutant risk to the treatment train and its supporting performance evidence. Gap to check A separator specification without the site and receiving-water assessment. Sources National standard 4.2 National standard 4.4 Industry guidance CIRIA C753 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-02 Provide a management train Requirement Provide a management train using source, site and regional controls as needed. Applies when All development. What to check Sequence of features on the layout. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-03 Higher-risk land uses Conditional Higher-risk uses may need proprietary treatment within the management train. Its evidence shall demonstrate necessary treatment throughout the development’s lifetime with appropriate maintenance. Very high-risk runoff requires discrete storage or treatment: where possible, discharge to a foul sewer under consent or use licensed off-site disposal. Environmental discharge is likely to require an EA permit. Applies when Commercial yards, lorry parks, fuel or chemical handling, industrial sites. What to check Pollution hazard, lifetime treatment evidence, maintenance, discrete facilities where needed, sewer consent or disposal route and any permit. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.7 National standard 4.8 National standard 4.9 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-04 Contain spills Requirement As far as reasonably practicable, design for interception and containment of a pollution incident, removal of contaminated water and rehabilitation of the system. High-risk cases, such as discharge to a designated site, may need isolation controls. Applies when All development; essential near designated sites. What to check Isolation points and access. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.11 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-05 Sediment remobilisation, climate resilience, amenity water Requirement Mitigate sediment washout in higher flows. Keep features effective under climate change. Water in public view should be clear and free of odour, sheen and litter. Applies when All development. What to check Sediment control and maintenance regime. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.5 National standard 4.10 National standard 4.12 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-06 Treat harvested water for its use Requirement Harvesting designs shall include the treatment needed for the intended use. Applies when Harvesting. What to check Treatment specification. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.13 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-07 Standard 4 applies to sewer discharges Requirement Standard 4 applies to discharges to surface water and combined sewers unless the sewerage undertaker sets stricter requirements. Applies when Sewer connections. What to check Treatment still provided. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.18 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Outfalls 2 checks WQ-08 Outfall hierarchy Recommendation Discharge to a water body should use, in order: an existing or new vegetated channel; reuse of an existing engineered outfall; a new engineered outfall designed for the watercourse hydromorphology. Applies when Discharge to a watercourse or the sea. What to check Justification for the outfall type. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.19 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-09 Outfall covers and tracing Recommendation New outfalls should allow pollution tracing, with access covers showing water type and flow direction. Applies when New outfalls. What to check Outfall detail. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.14 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Designated sites 2 checks WQ-10 Pollution prevention plan near the SAC Torbay criterion Demolition or major development within 250 m of the Lyme Bay and Torbay SAC, or near a watercourse with a hydrological link to it, needs a pollution prevention plan by a suitably qualified person covering soil and sediment runoff. Applies when Demolition or major development meeting the SAC trigger. What to check Plan submitted at validation. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources Torbay validation Validation List 3.12.1 Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-11 Local water improvement opportunities Requirement Consider reasonable and practical opportunities to improve receiving waters or support nutrient neutrality, proportionate to the scale of the development. This is a requirement to consider opportunities; it does not require every proposal to deliver an improvement. Applies when All applicable development, proportionate to scale. What to check Reference to the RBMP, DWMP or conservation objectives. Evidence to look for Land-use and receiving-water risk assessment; Treatment-train plan and supporting performance evidence; Spill containment, isolation and maintenance details Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 4.6 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Amenity and biodiversity
pages.lede: Multifunctional design, safety, planting and the biodiversity assessment. National standards 5 and 6.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment What the evidence should show How existing habitats, hydrology and site character informed the design. Mitigation, habitat connectivity, safe use and planting suited to the water conditions. The required final biodiversity evidence, with BNG addressed where applicable. Landscape context, public appreciation, accessible paths and usable space, with recreation where reasonably practicable; match the evidence to the proposal. Full evidence guide for this topic Annotated review examples Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Amenity 5 checks AB-01 Multifunctional design Requirement Adopt a SuDS approach that maximises amenity and demonstrates multifunctional water management. Keeping runoff at or near the surface is recommended. For surface features, high visual quality should have equal importance to functionality. Applies when All applicable development. What to check Multifunctional design evidence, landscape integration and the reason for any below-ground solution. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.1 National standard 5.2 National standard 5.3 National standard 5.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-02 Follow local landscape guidance Requirement Select and design features with regard to topography, existing flow routes, geodiversity, character, habitats, cultural and historical associations, infiltration and discharge potential. Inform the design by relevant LPA landscape guidance, character assessments, green infrastructure strategies, design policies and codes. Applies when All applicable development. What to check Site assessment and relevant Torbay landscape, green infrastructure and design documents. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.4 National standard 5.5 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-03 Planting, soils and biosecurity Conditional Where water is near the surface, vegetation and trees should be included as far as reasonably practicable. Species selection shall suit location, temperature, waterlogging and drought. Soil and aggregate specifications shall follow appropriate guidance. Planting operations shall comply with BS 3936-1:1992, BS 3936-10:1990 and BS 8545:2014, as specified in national footnote 32. Plant-selection guidance and sourcing that minimises biosecurity risks are recommendations. Applies when Vegetation or amenity features are proposed, with the recommendation to include vegetation applying where water is near the surface. What to check Planting schedule, species tolerance, soil and aggregate specification and compliance with the planting standards in national footnote 32. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.6 National standard 5.6.1 National standard 5.6.3 National standard 5.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-04 Public appreciation and recreation Requirement Convey or attenuate runoff in features that maximise public appreciation. Where proposals form part of a streetscape or public space, include leisure and recreation where reasonably practicable. Applies when All applicable development; the recreation requirement applies to streetscapes and public spaces. What to check Access, paths and usable space. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.8 National standard 5.9 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-05 Safety by design Requirement Apply good-practice principles to assess and manage risk in all cases. Shallow slopes, benching and margins are recommended for attenuation features. In community spaces, signage should explain function, public safety risks, benefits and authority contact details. Applies when All applicable development; apply the recommendations for attenuation features and community spaces where relevant. What to check Risk assessment and management, safe access, depths, side slopes and edges; signage and interpretation where appropriate. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.11 National standard 5.12 National standard 5.10 Topic evidence guide Link to this check Biodiversity 2 checks AB-06 Biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment at the outset Requirement Produce and agree a biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment at the start of design. It covers existing habitats and surveys, sensitivity, scale, local strategies (LNRS, RBMP) and BNG integration. Applies when All development, proportionate to scale and sensitivity. What to check An agreed assessment at the outset: surveys and baseline habitats; site and wider catchment effects; hydrological changes affecting habitats; scale and sensitivity; local strategies; impacts, mitigation and opportunities; biodiversity net gain integration where applicable. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment Identify baseline habitats and hydrology, effects, opportunities, mitigation and the required agreement with the approving body. Gap to check A general landscaping statement produced after drainage choices have already been fixed. Sources National standard 6.4 National standard 6.5 National standard 6.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-07 Show the final design adds biodiversity value Requirement Provide evidence that the design follows the biodiversity mitigation hierarchy and relevant designated-site requirements, delivers resilient and self-sustaining habitats and corridors, supports connectivity, considers invasive species and integrates with standards 1–5. Where contributing to biodiversity net gain, local nature recovery or nutrient credits, demonstrate current best practice. Applies when All development. What to check Evidence addressing every item in national standard 6.7, including ecology and drainage interactions, wider-catchment impacts, habitat connectivity and the required mitigation. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 6.2 National standard 6.6 National standard 6.7 National standard 6.8 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Construction, maintenance and adoption
pages.lede: Construction information, maintenance plans, access, failure, monitoring and structural integrity. National standard 7.
pages.text: What the labels mean Evidence for this topic Documents to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence What the evidence should show Who maintains each asset and how lifetime performance will be sustained. Practical access, rights, cleaning, replacement and failure response. Protection during construction, hydraulic operation through each phase and suitability for imposed loads. Full evidence guide for this topic Annotated review examples Match the document, revision and page to each check below. Maintenance 8 checks CM-01 Management and maintenance plan Requirement Provide a management and maintenance plan that sustains performance against standards 1–6 for the development’s lifetime. Torbay asks for the plan and an inspection checklist. The detailed management and maintenance contents in national standards 7.10–7.11 are recommendations. Applies when All applicable development; establish the delivery arrangements at outline and supply detail appropriate to the application stage. What to check Responsibilities and funding; asset and land ownership; easements; operating and pollution-incident instructions; establishment and routine maintenance; inspections, sediment and pollution controls and disposal; remedial work, replacement and post-flood rehabilitation. Evidence to look for Asset-specific management and maintenance plan Identify each asset, responsible party, lifetime arrangements and practical maintenance. Use the recommended contents in their stated context. Gap to check A generic schedule with no asset ownership or delivery arrangements. Sources National standard 7.2 National standard 7.10 National standard 7.11 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 6.0 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-02 Consider failure scenarios Requirement Examine the likelihood and consequences of operational failure, including blocked structures and controls and failed pumps. Evaluate both flood risk and water quality impacts and manage the risks. The design should make consequential blockage or clogging apparent from surface inspection. Applies when All development. What to check Flood-risk and water-quality failure assessment, safe operation and the means of detecting failure. Evidence to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.3 National standard 7.16 National standard 7.16.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-03 Access for maintenance Requirement Allow free, safe and easy access (with easements) for people, vehicles and machinery, including for emergencies. Applies when All development. What to check Access routes on the layout. Evidence to look for Maintenance access plan and sections Check that the maintenance activity and required equipment can reach each asset using the proposed route and rights. Gap to check A route labelled “access” without considering the actual task or obstructions. Sources National standard 7.12 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-04 Sediment removal Requirement Design the system so sediment, detritus and debris can be easily removed. Easily emptied, replaced or rehabilitated sediment controls are recommended where deposits could harm performance or design life. Establish the lawful waste classification, handling and disposal route for removed material. Applies when All development. What to check Access, sediment controls, removal method, waste classification and the applicable disposal requirements. Evidence to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.14 National standard 7.15 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-05 Automatic monitoring of pumps and proprietary products Conditional Where pumps or proprietary below-ground products (for example separators) are used, provide automatic monitoring and failure warnings to the responsible body. Applies when Pumps, separators and similar. What to check Telemetry specification. Evidence to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence.
