pages.title: Check a number
pages.lede: Compare runoff criteria and find the allowances and factors used in drainage assessments.
pages.text: Site maps and grid reference Locate a site and check the mapped constraints. No application needed. Compare key numbers Put document figures side by side and check differences and limits. Use these checks to compare the design inputs with the published criteria. Keep the calculation and the governing source with the application assessment. Compare runoff rates Use the entire development area that could drain to the proposed system in an extreme event, including permeable and impermeable surfaces. Enter its greenfield rates in litres per second, without climate change. The baseline greenfield volume also excludes climate change. For the volume test, compare the developed volume discharged to surface waters or sewers with greenfield runoff for the same event. Identify the volume remaining after interception, reuse or infiltration; generated runoff alone is not the comparison. Do not enter rates per hectare. Development area (ha) Greenfield 50% AEP rate (l/s) Greenfield 1% AEP rate (l/s) Greenfield 10% AEP rate (l/s), if available Greenfield 3.3% AEP rate (l/s), if available Volume discharged to surface waters or sewers in the developed 1% AEP, 6-hour event, compared with greenfield runoff National standards 3.18–3.20 apply the greater of the relevant greenfield rate and 3 l/s/ha. The comparison also shows the Torbay CDA criterion separately. It applies no automatic 1.5 l/s minimum and no brownfield relaxation. The national rate clauses do not prescribe a separate 3.3% AEP limit. The Torbay CDA comparison shows its applicable Q10 ceiling; the same event also checks on-site flooding. National standard 3.18 National standard 3.19 National standard 3.20 National standard 3.10 Torbay CDA advice CDA Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Read how the local 1.5 l/s minimum is handled . South Devon rainfall allowances National SuDS standard 3.8 requires the upper-end allowance, using the development lifetime and latest EA data. Torbay lies in the South Devon management catchment. Upper-end peak rainfall allowances for drainage design Epoch Period 3.3% AEP event 1% AEP event 2050s 2022–2060 35% 45% 2070s 2061–2125 40% 50% Record the development lifetime and selected epoch. Residential development should be assessed for a minimum 100-year lifetime. Where the lifetime extends beyond the published epoch, document how that period has been treated and establish the appropriate approach with the approving body. General flood risk assessment guidance also contains central allowances for specified lifetimes. Those values do not replace the upper-end requirement in SuDS standard 3.8. Torbay’s September 2022 guide states 50%; where a shorter-lifetime national value is lower, record and agree the treatment of the published local criterion. National standard 3.8 Environment Agency EA allowances Environment Agency EA allowance guidance Torbay infiltration factor of safety For the RP156 method, Torbay expects the national table’s “minor damage or inconvenience” values. Use 10 where failure would damage buildings or cause major inconvenience. Area drained (m²) Consequence of failure National standard National standards, table S3.1 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Interception criteria The first 5 mm criteria depend on the feature, lining, infiltration, contributing area, levels and outlet arrangement. Read all the conditions before applying a ratio. Check the feature-specific criteria Read national standard 2 in full .

pages.title: Rainwater harvesting
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Roofs with a dependable non-potable demand, such as toilet flushing or irrigation. What to consider The contributing area, rainfall, demand profile, storage, water quality, controls, overflow and safe separation from drinking water. Design limits A reliable demand is needed to empty storage between events. A tank that stays full cannot be assumed to provide storm storage. Maintenance Inspect filters, controls, tanks, pumps and overflow arrangements. Evidence to check Use a performance calculation appropriate to the design. Where claiming interception, check national standard 2; seasonal garden use alone does not demonstrate compliance. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 11 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks RD-09 Consider rainwater harvesting Conditional Rainwater harvesting shall be considered where there is a non-potable demand with enough catchment, a need for landscape irrigation, or the area is seriously water stressed. Applies when Any of the three triggers applies. Examples include industrial, commercial, educational, public sector, residential and multiple-occupancy buildings. What to check A reasoned demand assessment. If harvesting is not used, the reason. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.11 Local Plan Local Plan ER2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check RD-10 Design rainwater harvesting for its intended use Conditional Harvesting used to manage large rainfall events shall be designed to BS EN 16941. Harvesting design shall follow best practice and demonstrate effectiveness against a rainfall time series. Communal systems outside the curtilage shall consider public health and security. Applies when Rainwater harvesting is proposed; apply the large-event and communal-system conditions where relevant. What to check Rainfall time series, demand profile, applicable design standard and public health and security assessment. Evidence to look for Destination appraisal and catchment split plan; Ground evidence, levels and drainage long sections; Written discharge agreements and relevant land rights Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.12 National standard 1.13 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-07 Rainwater harvesting and water butts Conditional Surfaces draining to BS EN 16941 harvesting based on regular daily non-potable demand comply. Water butts limited to garden use in dry periods do not. Applies when Harvesting or water butts. What to check Daily demand basis; water butts not counted unless designed with calculations. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Green roofs
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Buildings where the structure, waterproofing and access can support the system. What to consider Roof loading, waterproofing, drainage layers, rainfall performance, safe access, fire considerations, plant choice and overflow. Design limits Roof loading and plant needs limit the suitable system. A green roof does not normally replace all downstream drainage. Maintenance Inspect outlets, vegetation, growing medium and waterproofing access points. Evidence to check A green roof draining only its own surface has a defined interception assumption in national standard 2.7. Show how excess runoff reaches the next feature. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 12 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks ER-06 Green roofs and walls Conditional Surfaces with green roofs or walls that drain only their own area comply. Applies when Green roofs or walls. What to check That no other area drains onto the roof. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-12 Design life and loading Requirement Show components last the development's design life (or include replacement in the plan) and resist design loads with factors of safety. Underground storage must suit the final surface use. Applies when All development. What to check Product specifications; structural adequacy of crates under parking. Evidence to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.4 National standard 7.24 National standard 7.25 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Infiltration features
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Sites with suitable infiltration rates, groundwater separation and acceptable ground risks. What to consider Testing at the feature location and depth, groundwater, contamination, stability, storage, safety factor, sediment control and overflow. Design limits Infiltration is sensitive to unsuitable ground, high groundwater and sediment. It can affect nearby structures or slopes. Maintenance Inspect inlets, sediment traps, access points and drawdown performance. Evidence to check Use the infiltration and groundwater requirements for the design evidence. Do not choose an infiltration feature from mapped soil conditions alone. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 13 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks IG-01 Prove infiltration with site testing Requirement Infiltration depends on suitable ground and adequate tested rates. Geotechnical investigation shall confirm the ground is suitable using recognised methods. Mapping can form an initial evidence base. Applies when Infiltration proposed, or evidence needed to assess its feasibility. Mapping can inform whether ground investigation is necessary. What to check Adequate site evidence for the hierarchy decision; location-specific investigation and testing where infiltration is relied on. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 1.14 National standard 1.14.1 National standard 3.14 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-02 Test to BRE 365 at the feature location and depth Torbay criterion Test in strict accordance with BRE 365 at the location and depth of each feature (or within 20 m where results are similar). Three consecutive tests to near emptying; extrapolation from 25% effective depth is not accepted. Permeable paving tested at 20 m intervals with pits at least 1.5 m × 1 m. Applies when All infiltration designs. What to check Test locations against the layout; three fills; full drainage. Evidence to look for Test plan and test records Match test locations, depths, logs and adopted infiltration rate to the proposed feature. Read the Torbay test criterion alongside the detailed ground evidence. Gap to check Unlocated test results or a test depth unrelated to the feature base. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-03 Keep 1 m above maximum groundwater Requirement The base of infiltration features shall be at least 1 m above the maximum likely groundwater level. For systems wholly relying on infiltration this 1 m unsaturated zone also protects groundwater. Applies when All infiltration. What to check Base level against groundwater evidence. Evidence to look for Groundwater evidence and feature section Show maximum likely groundwater and the proposed base on the same datum, with the separation demonstrated. Gap to check Groundwater depth quoted without relating it to the feature base. Sources National standard 1.15 National standard 4.16.1 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.1 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-07 Do not rely only on point infiltration below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s Requirement Point infiltration (for example soakaways) shall not be fully relied on where infiltration rates are below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s. Applies when Soakaways and other point features. What to check Tested rate. If lower, an additional destination. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.15 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-08 Half-empty within 24 hours Requirement Infiltration features shall half-empty their runoff volume within 24 hours for events up to the 3.3% AEP event. Applies when All infiltration features. What to check Half-drain time in the calculations. Evidence to look for Infiltration storage and half-drain calculation Identify the tested rate, storage geometry and safety factor used to demonstrate the stated half-drain performance. Gap to check A storage-volume result without a drain-time check. Sources National standard 3.16 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-09 Use the Torbay factor of safety Torbay criterion Size infiltration with the RP156 factor of safety. Torbay expects the 'minor damage to external areas or inconvenience' values: 2 for areas under 100 m², 3 for 100 to 1000 m², 5 for over 1000 m². Use 10 where failure would damage buildings or cause major inconvenience. Applies when Infiltration designed with the RP156 (CIRIA) method. What to check Factor used against drained area and consequence. Evidence to look for Calculation input and consequence assessment Trace the RP156 factor to the drained area and consequence of failure, and check it is applied in the calculation. Gap to check A factor stated in the narrative but absent or different in the calculation. Sources National standard 3.17 National standard National standards, table S3.1 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check ER-10 Infiltration trenches and soakaways Conditional Roads drained by infiltration trenches comply. Areas drained to systems designed to infiltrate 1-in-1-month events comply. Applies when Trenches and soakaways. What to check Design event for the infiltration system. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Filter strips
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Small adjacent drained areas with enough space to keep flow spread across the strip. What to consider Levels, contributing area, slope, vegetation, flow distribution and the next drainage feature. Design limits Concentrated flow can bypass treatment or erode the strip. Space and levels control effectiveness. Maintenance Maintain vegetation and remove sediment, litter and local erosion. Evidence to check Use as part of a management train. Show that runoff enters as distributed flow and where it goes afterwards. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 15 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks WQ-01 Base the treatment on a risk assessment Requirement Base the management train on a water quality risk assessment matched to the pollution hazard and receiving water sensitivity. Use the Simple Index Approach (C753) or another agreed method. Applies when All development. What to check Hazard level, sensitivity and treatment indices. Evidence to look for Pollution-risk and treatment assessment Trace land use, receptor sensitivity and pollutant risk to the treatment train and its supporting performance evidence. Gap to check A separator specification without the site and receiving-water assessment. Sources National standard 4.2 National standard 4.4 Industry guidance CIRIA C753 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-12 Protect infiltration surfaces from clogging Recommendation Features that infiltrate should include or be preceded by pre-treatment that protects the infiltration surface. Applies when All infiltration. What to check Silt traps, filter strips or other pre-treatment. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.13 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Filter drains
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Edges of roads, paths or landscaped areas where inspection and sediment management can be provided. What to consider Catchment, inlet arrangement, trench and pipe details, soil suitability, groundwater, treatment, overflow and access. Design limits Fine sediment can clog the stone and infiltration surface. A buried feature needs practical maintenance access. Maintenance Inspect and clean inlets, chambers and sediment controls; replace clogged material when necessary. Evidence to check State whether the feature conveys, stores or infiltrates runoff. Check the treatment needed before water reaches the drain. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 16 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks WQ-01 Base the treatment on a risk assessment Requirement Base the management train on a water quality risk assessment matched to the pollution hazard and receiving water sensitivity. Use the Simple Index Approach (C753) or another agreed method. Applies when All development. What to check Hazard level, sensitivity and treatment indices. Evidence to look for Pollution-risk and treatment assessment Trace land use, receptor sensitivity and pollutant risk to the treatment train and its supporting performance evidence. Gap to check A separator specification without the site and receiving-water assessment. Sources National standard 4.2 National standard 4.4 Industry guidance CIRIA C753 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-04 Sediment removal Requirement Design the system so sediment, detritus and debris can be easily removed. Easily emptied, replaced or rehabilitated sediment controls are recommended where deposits could harm performance or design life. Establish the lawful waste classification, handling and disposal route for removed material. Applies when All development. What to check Access, sediment controls, removal method, waste classification and the applicable disposal requirements. Evidence to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.14 National standard 7.15 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Swales
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Sites with suitable levels and enough width for safe side slopes, planting and maintenance. What to consider Gradient, check dams where useful, capacity, water quality, erosion, infiltration or lining, crossings and overflow. Design limits Steep gradients and concentrated inflows can cause erosion. Underground services and road crossings need coordination. Maintenance Manage vegetation, sediment, litter, erosion and inlet or outlet blockages. Evidence to check Check national standard 2.7 before claiming interception; the gradient, base material, contributing area and outlet arrangement matter. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 17 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks ER-09 Swales Conditional Fall under 1:100 with at least 500 mm suitable base: up to 5× the vegetated base area. Unlined, fall under 1:100 and over 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 25×. Steeper than 1:100: no interception unless shown by design. Areas draining within 5 m of an unlined swale outlet do not count unless the swale is flat with a raised outlet. Applies when Swales. What to check Long-section fall, base material, lining and outlet arrangement. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check WQ-01 Base the treatment on a risk assessment Requirement Base the management train on a water quality risk assessment matched to the pollution hazard and receiving water sensitivity. Use the Simple Index Approach (C753) or another agreed method. Applies when All development. What to check Hazard level, sensitivity and treatment indices. Evidence to look for Pollution-risk and treatment assessment Trace land use, receptor sensitivity and pollutant risk to the treatment train and its supporting performance evidence. Gap to check A separator specification without the site and receiving-water assessment. Sources National standard 4.2 National standard 4.4 Industry guidance CIRIA C753 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Rain gardens and bioretention
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Roofs, streets, car parks or small paved catchments where a planted feature fits the layout. What to consider Inflow, soil layers, storage depth, infiltration or underdrain, lining, planting, treatment and safe overflow. Design limits The feature needs suitable soil, a clear drainage route and enough space. Poor inflow details can cause erosion or uneven use. Maintenance Remove litter and sediment, maintain planting, inspect inlets and drains, and replace failing soil or plants. Evidence to check Show the area drained, the water-quality assessment and how the feature delivers interception. Lined and unlined systems need different evidence. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 18 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks ER-12 Bioretention and rain gardens Conditional Unlined bioretention complies where the impermeable area is up to 5× the vegetated surface receiving runoff (100 m² needs 20 m²). Applies when Rain gardens, bioretention, tree pits designed as bioretention. What to check Unlined; area ratio. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-03 Planting, soils and biosecurity Conditional Where water is near the surface, vegetation and trees should be included as far as reasonably practicable. Species selection shall suit location, temperature, waterlogging and drought. Soil and aggregate specifications shall follow appropriate guidance. Planting operations shall comply with BS 3936-1:1992, BS 3936-10:1990 and BS 8545:2014, as specified in national footnote 32. Plant-selection guidance and sourcing that minimises biosecurity risks are recommendations. Applies when Vegetation or amenity features are proposed, with the recommendation to include vegetation applying where water is near the surface. What to check Planting schedule, species tolerance, soil and aggregate specification and compliance with the planting standards in national footnote 32. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.6 National standard 5.6.1 National standard 5.6.3 National standard 5.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Trees and tree pits
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Streets and paved areas with space for roots, drainage layers and maintenance. What to consider Tree species, root space, soil, runoff quality, storage, drainage, lining, structural support and safe overflow. Design limits Roots, utilities, pavement loads and poor water quality can constrain the design. Avoid prolonged conditions unsuitable for the tree. Maintenance Care for the tree and soil, remove sediment and litter, and inspect inlet and overflow routes. Evidence to check Coordinate arboriculture, highway and drainage design. Show the hydraulic and treatment function rather than assuming any tree pit provides SuDS. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 19 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks ER-12 Bioretention and rain gardens Conditional Unlined bioretention complies where the impermeable area is up to 5× the vegetated surface receiving runoff (100 m² needs 20 m²). Applies when Rain gardens, bioretention, tree pits designed as bioretention. What to check Unlined; area ratio. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-03 Planting, soils and biosecurity Conditional Where water is near the surface, vegetation and trees should be included as far as reasonably practicable. Species selection shall suit location, temperature, waterlogging and drought. Soil and aggregate specifications shall follow appropriate guidance. Planting operations shall comply with BS 3936-1:1992, BS 3936-10:1990 and BS 8545:2014, as specified in national footnote 32. Plant-selection guidance and sourcing that minimises biosecurity risks are recommendations. Applies when Vegetation or amenity features are proposed, with the recommendation to include vegetation applying where water is near the surface. What to check Planting schedule, species tolerance, soil and aggregate specification and compliance with the planting standards in national footnote 32. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.6 National standard 5.6.1 National standard 5.6.3 National standard 5.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Permeable paving
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Paths, parking and other paved areas where structural loading and maintenance are compatible. What to consider Surface type, loads, sub-base, infiltration or lining, groundwater, additional contributing area, controls and overflow. Design limits Sediment and construction traffic can clog or damage the surface. Ground and vehicle use can require lining or additional treatment. Maintenance Inspect the surface, clean it using the appropriate method, and maintain outlets and access points. Evidence to check State whether the design is infiltrating, partially infiltrating or lined. Check standard 2.7 limits before claiming interception from adjacent paved areas. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 20 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks ER-08 Permeable surfaces Conditional No added area: complies (lined or unlined). Unlined with added impermeable area no greater than the permeable area: complies. Unlined over ground above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s: up to 5× the permeable area may be added (100 m² impermeable needs 20 m² permeable). Lined with added area: does not comply; add downstream interception. Applies when Permeable paving. What to check Lining, added area ratio and tested rate. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-11 Assess diffuse infiltration within 3 m of buildings Requirement Diffuse near-surface infiltration taking direct rainfall or a very small catchment similar in area to the infiltration surface should not normally pose a structural risk. Such proposals within 3 m of a building shall be assessed and mitigated where required. This reassurance does not extend to large contributing catchments. Applies when Permeable surfaces or similar within 3 m of a building. What to check Distance, contributing area relative to the infiltration surface, ground conditions, structural risk and any mitigation. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.27.2 Topic evidence guide Link to this check IG-14 Structural loading below trafficked surfaces Recommendation Where infiltration lies beneath trafficked surfaces, consider structural loading and soil weakening when saturated. Applies when Infiltration under roads or parking. What to check Structural design note. Evidence to look for Located investigation and test records; Groundwater and geotechnical evidence; Feature sections and infiltration calculations Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.26 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Attenuation tanks
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Sites needing temporary storage after reuse, infiltration and other measures have been assessed. What to consider Required volume, levels, inflows, outlet control, blockage protection, structural loads, access and exceedance. Design limits Storage alone does not deliver all seven standards. Underground tanks provide limited direct amenity and biodiversity. Maintenance Inspect and clean inlets, sediment controls, outlets and accessible storage areas. Evidence to check Choose above-ground and distributed storage where it fits the site. Explain interception and treatment separately, including safe access for repair and replacement. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 21 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks FE-01 No flooding up to 3.3% AEP plus climate change Requirement No flooding on any part of the site up to the 3.3% AEP (1 in 30 year) event plus climate change, unless the area is designed to hold or convey water. Applies when All development. What to check Model results for the 3.3% AEP + cc event. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.35 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-02 Protect buildings, plant and escape routes up to 1% AEP plus climate change Requirement No flooding of buildings (including basements), utility plant susceptible to water, or safe access and escape routes up to the 1% AEP event plus climate change. Manage any system flooding within the development. Applies when All development. What to check Flood volumes and locations for 1% AEP + cc against levels. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 3.36 National standard 3.5 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check FE-03 Below-ground storage: suggested modelling approaches Recommendation Where there is no above-ground storage, Torbay suggests either: 1) 1% AEP + cc with top water level below the incoming pipe invert; or 2) 1% AEP with no flooding, and 3.3% AEP + cc top water level below the incoming pipe invert. Applies when Systems with only below-ground storage. What to check Top water level against incoming invert. Evidence to look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections; Event results identifying flooded and protected locations; Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. These are suggested modelling approaches. They do not replace the applicable national climate-adjusted performance, flooding and protected-receptor checks in FE-01 and FE-02. Sources Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.3 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-12 Design life and loading Requirement Show components last the development's design life (or include replacement in the plan) and resist design loads with factors of safety. Underground storage must suit the final surface use. Applies when All development. What to check Product specifications; structural adequacy of crates under parking. Evidence to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.4 National standard 7.24 National standard 7.25 Torbay guidance SuDS guide 4.4 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Detention basins
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits A shallow basin can store runoff above ground and release it at a controlled rate. An unlined basin may also deliver infiltration and interception where the ground and design allow. What to examine Check inlet and outlet levels, storage, vegetation, sediment management, safe slopes, access, exceedance routes and maintenance. The area below the outlet matters when claiming interception. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 22 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks ER-11 Detention basins Conditional A flat, unlined vegetated basin base below the outlet, without specific provision routing low flows directly to the outlet, can receive up to five times that base area. Above 1×10⁻⁶ m/s infiltration, the ratio can be up to 25:1. Higher ratios need justification using below-outlet storage, higher infiltration rates and detailed design. Provide upstream sediment control for infiltrating basins. Applies when Detention basins. What to check Effective below-outlet base area, lining, levels, low-flow routing, tested infiltration and sediment control; calculations for a higher ratio. Evidence to look for Basin catchment plan and section Identify effective receiving area, lining, infiltration, low-flow route and levels below the outlet. Test every applicable basin condition. Gap to check An area ratio alone, or storage above the outlet used to prove interception. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-05 Safety by design Requirement Apply good-practice principles to assess and manage risk in all cases. Shallow slopes, benching and margins are recommended for attenuation features. In community spaces, signage should explain function, public safety risks, benefits and authority contact details. Applies when All applicable development; apply the recommendations for attenuation features and community spaces where relevant. What to check Risk assessment and management, safe access, depths, side slopes and edges; signage and interpretation where appropriate. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.11 National standard 5.12 National standard 5.10 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Ponds and wetlands
pages.lede: Design considerations, maintenance and the relevant assessment checks.
pages.text: Where it fits Sites with enough land, suitable levels and a reliable design for water balance and safety. What to consider Permanent pool, temporary storage, water quality, planting, sediment removal, safe slopes, access and downstream controls. Design limits Water levels, seasonal drying, public access, sediment and habitat needs require coordinated design. Maintenance Manage sediment, vegetation, litter, water quality, control structures and access. Evidence to check A permanent-pool attenuation pond is not assumed to provide interception under standard 2.7. Provide upstream interception and treatment where needed. Check the full drainage requirements and lifetime maintenance arrangements for the proposed system. Detailed component design: CIRIA C753, chapter 23 . Read alongside the current national standards below. Relevant assessment checks ER-13 Attenuation ponds give no interception Conditional Areas drained by attenuation ponds with a permanent pool are assumed not to deliver interception. Applies when Wet ponds. What to check Interception provided upstream instead. Evidence to look for Positively drained surface schedule and catchment plan; Interception calculations or evidence for the applicable simplified approach; Feature sections, area schedules and any required agreement Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. This is a compliance presumption for the proposed feature, not a requirement to provide it. Apply the agreement and calculation conditions in ER-05 and national standards 2.6.2–2.7. Sources National standard 2.7 Topic evidence guide Link to this check AB-05 Safety by design Requirement Apply good-practice principles to assess and manage risk in all cases. Shallow slopes, benching and margins are recommended for attenuation features. In community spaces, signage should explain function, public safety risks, benefits and authority contact details. Applies when All applicable development; apply the recommendations for attenuation features and community spaces where relevant. What to check Risk assessment and management, safe access, depths, side slopes and edges; signage and interpretation where appropriate. Evidence to look for Early biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment; Coordinated ecology, landscape, planting and drainage drawings; Final biodiversity evidence and safety assessment Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 5.11 National standard 5.12 National standard 5.10 Topic evidence guide Link to this check CM-07 Minimise energy and prioritise source control Requirement As far as reasonably practicable, minimise energy use over the design life. Prioritise source control to minimise large downstream attenuation ponds with safety-critical maintenance requirements. Applies when All development. What to check Distribution of features; pumping avoided. Evidence to look for Asset-specific maintenance plan and inspection information; Ownership, adoption and usable access arrangements; Construction, phasing, commissioning and structural evidence Gap to check The conclusion cannot be traced to the submitted design or supporting evidence. Sources National standard 7.17 National standard 7.23 Topic evidence guide Link to this check

pages.title: Outline application
pages.lede: Establish a deliverable strategy, drainage destination, space and key constraints.
pages.text: Information to check An outline proposal needs a feasible surface-water drainage strategy. Resolve the drainage principles and land requirements before fixing development parameters. Use these headings to check the submission. Record findings against the application reference . Site and catchment information Location, boundary, levels, drainage catchments, existing drains, watercourses, outfalls and constraints. Flood risk assessment Assess all relevant flood sources, future climate and safe site operation. Use a proportionate assessment for the proposal. Feasible runoff destination Assess the hierarchy and provide enough evidence to establish a deliverable outfall and discharge arrangement. Concept drainage layout Reserve realistic space and levels for the management train, treatment, storage, access and safe flow routes. Initial infiltration and groundwater evidence Establish whether infiltration is feasible and what site investigations remain necessary for the detailed design. Indicative rates, volumes and storage Demonstrate the strategy can satisfy the national and local criteria, including climate change and urban creep. National standards statement Explain how all seven national SuDS standards are met. Record and justify any departure and the agreement sought. Interception and treatment evidence Identify contributing surfaces, first 5 mm interception and the water-quality assessment and treatment train. Amenity and biodiversity Include the biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment produced and agreed at the outset under standard 6.4. Coordinate drainage, landscape and ecology; explain benefits and safety. Outline maintenance and delivery plan Identify the proposed owner, maintenance route, funding approach, phasing and the timetable for detailed evidence. Plain-language strategy summary Summarise the site constraints, proposed solution, key assumptions and evidence that the strategy fits the layout. Sequential and exception tests where applicable Check current NPPF F5 and F6, their exemptions and the local validation requirements. Provide the evidence needed for this proposal and stage. Pollution prevention plan where applicable For demolition or major development, check the 250 m Lyme Bay and Torbay SAC buffer and nearby watercourses with a hydrological link. Include the qualified-person plan required by Local Validation List 3.12.1. Keep documents consistent Use drawing numbers and revisions. Coordinate the drainage information with the layout, levels, landscape and ecology plans. Provide a clear record of changes. Planning submission Use Torbay's national and local validation requirements for the complete application list. Apply for planning permission

pages.title: Full application
pages.lede: Check the coordinated design, calculations, treatment and lifetime delivery.
pages.text: Information to check A full proposal needs a detailed surface-water drainage scheme, with evidence that the whole system can be built and perform as designed. Use these headings to check the submission. Record findings against the application reference . Site and catchment information Location, boundary, levels, drainage catchments, existing drains, watercourses, outfalls and constraints. Flood risk assessment Assess all relevant flood sources, future climate and safe site operation. Use a proportionate assessment for the proposal. Runoff destination and agreements Show how higher-priority destinations have been maximised, the selected outfall, capacity, discharge parameters and rights. Infiltration tests and groundwater evidence Provide location- and depth-specific testing, seasonal groundwater evidence and contamination and stability assessments where relevant. National standards statement Explain how all seven national SuDS standards are met. Record and justify any departure and the agreement sought. Interception and treatment evidence Identify contributing surfaces, first 5 mm interception and the water-quality assessment and treatment train. Hydraulic design and storage Show existing and proposed rates and volumes, rainfall data, climate allowance, urban creep, event results and critical storage durations. Drainage layout and levels Identify each feature, pipe connection, flow control, outfall, ground level, floor level and available storage. Safe exceedance and failure routes Map flows beyond the design event, blocked controls, surcharged outfalls and flood-locking; show effects on and off site. Amenity and biodiversity Include the biodiversity risk and opportunity assessment produced and agreed at the outset under standard 6.4. Coordinate drainage, landscape and ecology; explain benefits and safety. Ownership and maintenance Identify lifetime ownership, tasks, access, inspections, replacement responsibilities and funding. Construction details and phased delivery Provide feature and control details, connecting-network information, construction protection, temporary drainage and commissioning arrangements. Technical and non-technical summaries Provide calculation inputs and outputs, plus a clear explanation of the design and the conclusions. Coordinate the drainage information with the layout, levels, landscape and ecology plans. Provide a clear record of changes. Planning submission Use Torbay's national and local validation requirements for the complete application list. Apply for planning permission

pages.lede: Use evidence proportionate to the proposal and the applicable planning route.
pages.text: Householder applications Torbay’s validation list requires a flood risk assessment including a surface water drainage strategy. For most householder proposals in Flood Zone 1, use the council’s short flood risk assessment proforma where appropriate. Check the form’s conditions and the actual flood and drainage risks. Prior approval and change of use Identify the precise permitted-development or application route and the matters that can be considered. The validation list includes flood risk information for relevant prior approvals. Establish whether the proposal alters impermeable area, discharge, drainage operation or flood vulnerability. Keep the evidence proportionate Check the site, destination, infiltration, receiving system, flood routes and maintenance as relevant. A smaller application does not automatically remove a substantive requirement. Record the reason where a technical check does not apply. pages.title: Other drainage permissions
pages.lede: Identify the permissions needed for watercourses, connections, highways and discharge.
pages.text: Ordinary watercourses An ordinary watercourse is a stream, ditch, drain or other watercourse that is not designated as a main river. Torbay Council is the consenting authority for ordinary watercourses in its area. Obstructions, new culverts and alterations to culverts that affect flow require written consent under the Land Drainage Act. Include temporary works in the assessment. Obtain consent before starting; there is no retrospective consent route. Read Torbay's consent guidance and application route . Main rivers and flood defences Check the Environment Agency's main river designation. Works in or near main rivers, flood defences or associated structures can require a flood-risk activity permit. Check the Environment Agency flood-risk activity permit requirements . Sewers, highways and land rights Agree sewer connections and receiving capacity with the sewerage undertaker. In Torbay, use South West Water's building and development services . Agree highway drainage, works and adoption arrangements with the highway authority where relevant. Secure landowner permission and lifetime rights for drainage on or across third-party land. Check environmental discharge permits and groundwater protection requirements with the Environment Agency. Protect existing watercourses National policy F8 seeks to keep existing open watercourses open unless there are compelling reasons for enclosure. It also supports removing culverts and restoring channels where this can be done without increased flood risk, environmental harm or harm to heritage assets. Keep access for inspection and maintenance and demonstrate how the watercourse and receiving system will operate.

pages.title: How SuDS work
pages.lede: Manage rainfall near where it falls, using features that slow, store, treat or reuse it.
pages.text: What sustainable drainage does Development changes how rainwater moves. Roofs, roads and paving can increase the amount and speed of runoff. SuDS manage that water using a natural approach, with features distributed through the site. A system can include rainwater reuse, planted areas, permeable paving, channels, ponds and storage. The right combination depends on the ground, levels, available space and the receiving drainage system. How the features work together Manage water near its source. Reuse it or direct it into a suitable local feature. Slow and treat the flow. Use soil, vegetation and sediment controls as part of a treatment train. Store larger flows. Keep enough capacity for the design rainfall and release runoff at an acceptable rate. Provide a safe route for excess water. Protect buildings, people and surrounding land if capacity is exceeded. The benefits to check The national standards combine flood-risk control with water quality, amenity, biodiversity and lifetime maintenance. Good design considers these together from the start. Use drainage requirements for the criteria and SuDS features for the design choices.

pages.title: Drainage glossary
pages.lede: Find plain-language definitions of the terms used in this guide.
pages.text: Curtilage Land around a building or group of buildings forming one enclosure for occupants’ private use. It need not equal the application red-line boundary. National glossary · Urban creep check RV-11 . Annual exceedance probability AEP The chance that a rainfall or flood event of a stated size will be exceeded in any one year. A 1% annual chance is commonly called a 1 in 100 year event. Amenity The benefit a place provides to people, such as useful open space, enjoyment and an attractive setting. Attenuation Temporary storage that slows the rate at which runoff is released. Biodiversity The variety of living things and habitats. Bioretention A planted drainage feature using soil or engineered media to store and treat runoff. Rain gardens can be bioretention features. Brownfield Previously developed land. Its existing drainage does not automatically set an acceptable new discharge rate. Catchment The area from which water drains to a particular point or system. Combined sewer A sewer receiving both foul sewage and surface-water runoff. Critical drainage area CDA An area identified by the Environment Agency as having critical drainage problems. Design event The rainfall event used to check drainage performance, including the specified climate allowance. Exceedance Flow occurring when rainfall or other conditions exceed the drainage system's design capacity. Flood locking When high water levels at an outfall prevent or reduce drainage discharge. Freeboard A vertical margin between a design water level and a level that needs protection. Greenfield runoff Estimated runoff from the site in its undeveloped state, used as a design comparison. Infiltration Water soaking into the ground. Interception Keeping runoff from leaving the site through reuse, infiltration or loss to the atmosphere. Lead Local Flood Authority LLFA The authority with local flood-risk responsibilities. Torbay Council is the LLFA for Torbay. Management train A linked sequence of drainage features that controls and treats runoff. Non-potable water Water used for a purpose that does not require drinking-water quality, such as toilet flushing. Outfall The point where a drainage system discharges water. Qbar and Qmed Statistical estimates of typical annual flood flow used in runoff assessment. National standard 3.27 allows either as an equivalent 50% annual-chance greenfield rate. Rainwater harvesting Collecting and storing rainfall for use. Runoff Water that flows over or drains from a surface after rain. SuDS Sustainable drainage systems: features that manage surface water using a natural approach and provide several benefits. Surface-water sewer A sewer intended to carry surface-water runoff, rather than foul sewage. Surcharge When the water level rises above the inside top of the pipe (its soffit), so the pipe flows under pressure. Surcharge does not necessarily mean water reaches the ground surface; surface flooding occurs when water escapes onto the surface. Water UK Appendix C v2.2, C6.2.3 note (printed page 57) . Urban creep Additional hard surfaces introduced over time, such as paving private gardens.

pages.title: Evidence guides
pages.lede: Choose a topic to see the evidence to look for.

pages.text: Look for Site-specific flood risk assessment and dated map extracts Topographical survey, proposed levels, access drawings and any applicable emergency plan Flood-zone compatibility, applicable sequential or exception test evidence, and coastal-risk assessment where relevant The evidence should demonstrate The site boundary, relevant present and future flood sources, coastal risk where applicable, and the development lifetime. How floor levels, safe access, residual risk and resilience relate to assessed flood conditions. The precise basis for each planning test, exemption, compatibility finding and CDA interpretation. Common gaps A Flood Zone screenshot used as the entire assessment. “Low risk” or “safe access” stated without the relevant flood conditions and levels. pages.title: Infiltration and groundwater evidence

pages.text: Look for Located investigation and test records Groundwater and geotechnical evidence Feature sections and infiltration calculations The evidence should demonstrate Tests representative of the proposed feature locations and depths, with a traceable design rate. Common gaps Unlocated tests or a geology map used as proof of detailed performance. A dry-season groundwater observation treated as the maximum likely level. pages.title: Everyday rainfall evidence

Common gaps Naming a rain garden without its dimensions or catchment. Treating attenuation storage or permanent pond water as interception. Applying an area ratio without the other qualifying conditions. Record the finding Identify the document, revision, drawing or page. Explain which part of the check the evidence supports and what remains unresolved. A document title or completed template does not establish that its contents meet the criterion. pages.title: Runoff rates, volumes and storage evidence

Common gaps One peak-flow result without the required volume comparison. Existing brownfield discharge used as the greenfield baseline. A minimum discharge rate applied automatically. Model areas, levels or storage that do not match the drawings. Record the finding Identify the document, revision, drawing or page. pages.title: Flooding and exceedance evidence
pages.lede: The documents and findings that support the assessment.
pages.text: Look for Levelled exceedance plan and relevant sections Event results identifying flooded and protected locations Outfall, blockage, surcharge and failure assessments The evidence should demonstrate Where water moves when capacity is exceeded and the consequences at site boundaries. The relationship between water levels, buildings, vulnerable plant and escape routes. The effects of incoming runoff, submerged outfalls, blockage and justified freeboard. Common gaps Arrows without supporting levels. “No flooding” without identifying the locations protected. Normal-operation results used to dismiss blockage or flood-locking. Record the finding Identify the document, revision, drawing or page. Explain which part of the check the evidence supports and what remains unresolved. pages.title: Can this site use infiltration?
pages.lede: Establish the ground evidence before relying on infiltration or moving down the destination hierarchy.
pages.text: This route identifies the checks and evidence to examine. Record the finding against the application; the answers do not grant an approval or create an exemption. Read all the guidance in this route What does the initial site evidence show? Infiltration may be feasible A site constraint may rule it out There is not enough evidence Establish the initial ground evidence Review mapping, available investigations, geology, groundwater, contamination and stability. Initial mapping can inform whether further investigation is necessary; it is not proof of a detailed infiltration design. IG-01 · Prove infiltration with site testing RD-02 · Evidence for using a lower destination Is the reason for discounting infiltration supported by site evidence? Yes — the evidence explains the constraint No, or uncertain Record the constraint and the hierarchy appraisal Record why infiltration cannot be used, whether any part remains practicable, and the evidence supporting the next destination. Where contamination is the constraint, assess practicable remediation together with the drainage design before discounting a higher destination. Testing is not automatically necessary where adequate initial evidence establishes that it is not needed. RD-02 · Evidence for using a lower destination RD-03 · Maximise each destination in order RD-04 · Contamination is not an automatic reason to move down IG-01 · Prove infiltration with site testing IG-05 · No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding Are detailed tests and ground evidence relevant to the proposed locations and depths? Yes No, or not supplied Obtain the ground evidence needed for the proposed design Check the Torbay test method, proposed locations and depths, and relevant seasonal groundwater evidence. Identify stability and pollution risks before accepting a design rate. IG-02 · Test to BRE 365 at the feature location and depth IG-04 · Establish wet-winter groundwater levels IG-05 · No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding IG-13 · Groundwater protection and contaminated land Are groundwater separation, stability and pollution risks demonstrated? Yes No, or uncertain Resolve the ground constraints Read the feature sections and ground assessment together. A favourable infiltration rate alone does not establish safe groundwater separation, stability or pollution performance. IG-03 · Keep 1 m above maximum groundwater IG-05 · No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding IG-10 · Assess point infiltration within 5 m of structures IG-11 · Assess diffuse infiltration within 3 m of buildings IG-13 · Groundwater protection and contaminated land Check the complete infiltration design Verify adopted rate, method, factor of safety and half-drain performance. Check the applicable requirements and recommendations for clogging protection, loading and exceedance. Record the finding against the evidence; this route does not approve a soakaway. IG-07 · Do not rely only on point infiltration below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s IG-08 · Half-empty within 24 hours IG-09 · Use the Torbay factor of safety IG-12 · Protect infiltration surfaces from clogging IG-14 · Structural loading below trafficked surfaces FE-09 · Exceedance routes

pages.title: Which discharge criteria apply?
pages.lede: Keep the national event and volume tests separate from the applicable local criteria.
pages.text: This route identifies the checks and evidence to examine. Record the finding against the application; the answers do not grant an approval or create an exemption. Read all the guidance in this route Where is the proposed discharge going? Infiltration Watercourse or sewer Tidal water or the sea The destination is not established Check infiltration performance and overflow Use the infiltration checks for the proposed system. Identify any positive overflow or alternative discharge route and assess its applicable criteria separately. IG-01 · Prove infiltration with site testing IG-08 · Half-empty within 24 hours IG-09 · Use the Torbay factor of safety RD-17 · Ask for a fallback destination Assess the receiving-water exception and local context Read the national exception for tidal or sea discharges, then assess tide-locking, receiving conditions, pollution, local controls and necessary agreements. Do not assume a coastal location creates an unrestricted outfall. RV-08 · Tidal or sea outfalls FE-07 · Surcharged outfalls and flood-locking WQ-08 · Outfall hierarchy RD-11 · Agree discharge to a watercourse in writing Establish a deliverable destination first Follow the destination hierarchy and identify the receiving system, route, capacity, rights and required agreements before selecting design discharge criteria. RD-01 · Follow the destination hierarchy RD-02 · Evidence for using a lower destination RD-05 · Secure rights over third-party land RD-11 · Agree discharge to a watercourse in writing RD-12 · Agree sewer connections in writing with capacity Is the volume discharged to surface waters or sewers in the developed 1% AEP, six-hour event greater than greenfield runoff for the same event? Yes No Not established Use the increased-volume national branch, then compare local criteria National clauses 3.18 and 3.19 use the greater of the 50% AEP greenfield rate and 3 l/s/ha for the relevant rate tests. Check the contributing area and baseline, then compare applicable local event-specific greenfield criteria and the Q10 ceiling. Record source differences and any agreement. RV-03 · 50% AEP limit RV-04 · 1% AEP limit: volume test RV-05 · Compare the applicable national and local limits RV-06 · Check proposals relying on the published 1.5 l/s minimum RV-07 · Brownfield sites: check the greenfield expectation Use the no-increase national branch, then compare local criteria The national 50% AEP test uses the greater of its greenfield rate and 3 l/s/ha. Clause 3.20 uses the greater of the 1% AEP greenfield rate and 3 l/s/ha for the 1% test. Compare applicable local criteria separately and record the governing basis. RV-03 · 50% AEP limit RV-04 · 1% AEP limit: volume test RV-05 · Compare the applicable national and local limits RV-06 · Check proposals relying on the published 1.5 l/s minimum RV-07 · Brownfield sites: check the greenfield expectation Obtain the discharged-volume comparison The 1% AEP national limit cannot be established from peak-rate figures alone. Compare greenfield runoff volume with the developed volume discharged to surface waters or sewers. Distinguish runoff generated from the volume remaining after interception, reuse or infiltration. Check the entire area potentially draining to the system and the correct model inputs. RV-04 · 1% AEP limit: volume test RV-09 · Greenfield runoff method RV-14 · Model the SuDS and pipes together

FE-03 · Below-ground storage: suggested modelling approaches Local checks in detail FR-01 Check the critical drainage area boundary Officer guidance Use the Torbay CDA criteria for conservative screening across Torbay. For a site in Maidencombe, establish the current EA designation and boundary before relying on CDA status in a formal assessment. Applies when All development that could affect drainage. What to check The site against the current designation map, the applicable local policy and any written confirmation of the 2026 extension. Record the boundary and the basis of the assessment. Evidence to look for Dated designation map and recorded assessment basis Locate the application boundary and identify the source version. For Maidencombe, record the published source difference and the confirmation relied on. Gap to check A general statement that the whole borough is designated, without addressing the boundary evidence. Local interpretation Sources differ. The Local Plan (2015) and SFRA Level 1 (June 2026) say the whole of Torbay is a CDA. The Validation List (November 2024) and the draft SFRA Level 2A (June 2026) say Maidencombe is outside it. The EA national dataset published in September 2026 has a July 2025 geometry revision and does not establish the extension. Whole-Torbay screening is the working interpretation, not confirmation of a new formal boundary. The local Validation List still requires an FRA in Maidencombe.
